|style="text-align:center;" colspan=2|[[Mike Smith (American football coach)|Mike Smith]]
|style="text-align:center;"|Fired
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Dan Quinn (American football)|Dan Quinn]]
|Smith compiled a record of 67–50 (.573), including the postseason, in seven seasons with the Falcons. He is the only coach to lead the franchise to consecutive winning seasons and consecutive playoff berths.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Patra|first1=Kevin|title=Atlanta Falcons fire coach Mike Smith|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/atlanta-falcons-fire-coach-mike-smith-0ap3000000451246|work=NFL.com|access-date=29 September 2014|archive-date=March 17, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150317094252/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000451246/article/atlanta-falcons-fire-coach-mike-smith|url-status=live}}</ref>

Quinn, who never held a head coaching position prior to 2015, had served as defensive coordinator for the [[Seattle Seahawks]]. Due to league anti-[[tapping up|tampering]] rules, the Falcons had to wait until after the completion of the Seahawks' playoff run, before formally hiring Quinn.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/12266193/dan-quinn-atlanta-falcons-introduction|title=Falcons to introduce Dan Quinn|last=McClure|first=Vaughan|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 2, 2015|website=ESPN.com|access-date=April 25, 2015|archive-date=July 20, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190720050122/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/12266193/dan-quinn-atlanta-falcons-introduction|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Buffalo Bills]]
|style="text-align:center;" colspan=2|[[Doug Marrone]]
|style="text-align:center;"|Resigned
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Rex Ryan]]
|Marrone compiled a record of 15–17 (.469) in two seasons with the Bills and resigned on December 31, 2014.<ref>[http://www.allsportswny.com/statement-from-buffalo-bills-owner-terry-pegula-regarding-marrone-opt-out/ Statement from Buffalo Bills owner Terry Pegula regarding Marrone opt-out] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150102222123/http://www.allsportswny.com/statement-from-buffalo-bills-owner-terry-pegula-regarding-marrone-opt-out/ |date=January 2, 2015 }}. ''WBBZ-TV''. Retrieved December 31, 2014.</ref> His tenure was marked by the team's first winning season since 2004 but also by tensions with general manager [[Doug Whaley]] and players, especially [[Mike Williams (wide receiver, born 1987)|Mike Williams]], who requested a trade during the season. Marrone's contract had an opt-out clause which allowed him to resign his position within three days of the end of the season and still collect his full salary for the rest of the contract (he had one year remaining) if the team changed ownership which it did when the Bills were sold to the Pegula family in September. Marrone joined the Jacksonville Jaguars as offensive line coach.<ref>Long, Mark (January 20, 2015). [http://www.oleantimesherald.com/sports/article_40438a42-a137-11e4-b975-2baea0124b48.html Jaguars hire Marrone as assistant head coach] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702135332/http://www.oleantimesherald.com/sports/article_40438a42-a137-11e4-b975-2baea0124b48.html |date=July 2, 2019 }}. ''Associated Press''. Retrieved January 21, 2015.</ref>

On January 12, 2015, the Bills hired [[Rex Ryan]] as their head coach. Ryan had spent the previous six seasons as head coach of the New York Jets.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Patra|first1=Kevin|title=Buffalo Bills hire Rex Ryan as head coach|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/buffalo-bills-hire-rex-ryan-as-head-coach-0ap3000000456519|website=NFL.com|access-date=12 January 2015|archive-date=April 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170422072518/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000456519/article/buffalo-bills-hire-rex-ryan-as-head-coach|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Chicago Bears]]
|style="text-align:center;" colspan=2|[[Marc Trestman]]
|style="text-align:center;"|Fired
|style="text-align:center;"|[[John Fox (American football)|John Fox]]
|Trestman compiled a record of 13–19 (.406) in two seasons with the Bears, and had finished the 2014 season with a 5–11 record. He and general manager [[Phil Emery (American football)|Phil Emery]] were both dismissed on December 29, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Rosenthal|first1=Gregg|title=Chicago Bears fire Marc Trestman|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/chicago-bears-fire-marc-trestman-0ap3000000451258|work=NFL.com|access-date=29 September 2014|archive-date=December 29, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141229171803/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000451258/article/chicago-bears-fire-marc-trestman|url-status=live}}</ref> Trestman then became offensive coordinator for the Baltimore Ravens.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/ravens-hire-marc-trestman-as-offensive-coordinator-0ap3000000461175 |title=Ravens hire Marc Trestman as offensive coordinator |work=NFL.com |access-date=2015-05-19 |archive-date=October 5, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241005063325/https://www.nfl.com/news/ravens-hire-marc-trestman-as-offensive-coordinator-0ap3000000461175 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Fox was hired on January 16, 2015, to become the head coach. Fox spent the past 4 seasons as the head coach of the Denver Broncos.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Sessler|first1=Marc|title=Chicago Bears hire John Fox as head coach|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/chicago-bears-hire-john-fox-as-head-coach-0ap3000000459551|website=NFL.com|access-date=17 January 2015|archive-date=June 18, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240618224355/https://www.nfl.com/news/chicago-bears-hire-john-fox-as-head-coach-0ap3000000459551|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Denver Broncos]]
|style="text-align:center;" colspan=2|[[John Fox (American football)|John Fox]]
|style="text-align:center;"|Mutual decision
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Gary Kubiak]]
|In four seasons with the Broncos, Fox compiled a record of 49–22 (.690) including postseason games, won his division all four seasons, and appeared in [[Super Bowl XLVIII]], but was bounced from the playoffs in the divisional round the other three years. By mutual agreement, Fox left the team on January 12, 2015, following the most recent divisional playoff loss.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Wesseling|first1=Chris|title=John Fox, Denver Broncos part ways after four years|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/john-fox-denver-broncos-part-ways-after-four-seasons-0ap3000000457308|website=NFL.com|access-date=12 January 2015|archive-date=January 13, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150113005134/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000457308/article/john-fox-denver-broncos-part-ways|url-status=live}}</ref>

Kubiak was hired on January 19, 2015, to become the head coach. Kubiak, formerly head coach of the [[Houston Texans]] from 2006 to 2013, spent the past season as the offensive coordinator of the Baltimore Ravens.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Patra|first1=Kevin|title=Gary Kubiak hired as Denver Broncos head coach|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/gary-kubiak-hired-as-denver-broncos-head-coach-0ap3000000460494|website=NFL.com|access-date=20 January 2015|archive-date=May 6, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506135311/https://www.nfl.com/news/gary-kubiak-hired-as-denver-broncos-head-coach-0ap3000000460494|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
|style="text-align:center;"|[[New York Jets]]
|style="text-align:center;" colspan=2|[[Rex Ryan]]
|style="text-align:center;" |Fired
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Todd Bowles]]
|Ryan compiled a record of 50–52 (.490), including postseason games, in six seasons as head coach of the Jets. Ryan led the Jets to two [[AFC Championship Game]] appearances in his first two seasons, losing both, but failed to earn a winning season or playoff berth in his last four. He and general manager [[John Idzik, Jr.]] were both dismissed on December 29, 2014.<ref name=NYJfire>{{cite web|last1=Orr|first1=Conor|title=New York Jets fire Rex Ryan, John Idzik|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/new-york-jets-fire-rex-ryan-john-idzik-0ap3000000451236|website=NFL.com|access-date=9 January 2015|archive-date=April 4, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240404232714/https://www.nfl.com/news/new-york-jets-fire-rex-ryan-john-idzik-0ap3000000451236|url-status=live}}</ref>

Bowles was hired on January 14, 2015, to become their head coach after serving as defensive coordinator for Arizona Cardinals since 2013; he previously served as interim head coach of the Miami Dolphins in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Wesseling|first1=Chris|title=New York Jets hiring Todd Bowles as head coach|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/new-york-jets-announce-todd-bowles-as-head-coach-0ap3000000458689|website=NFL.com|access-date=14 January 2015|archive-date=June 19, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240619131612/https://www.nfl.com/news/new-york-jets-announce-todd-bowles-as-head-coach-0ap3000000458689|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Oakland Raiders]]
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Dennis Allen (American football)|Dennis Allen]]
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Tony Sparano]]
|style="text-align:center;"|Fired
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Jack Del Rio]]
|Allen was fired on September 29, 2014, after an 8–28 (.222) record as Raiders head coach, and an 0–4 start to the 2014 season.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Rosenthal|first1=Gregg|title=Raiders fire Dennis Allen after two-plus seasons|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/raiders-fire-dennis-allen-after-two-plus-seasons-0ap3000000403246|website=NFL.com|access-date=29 September 2014|archive-date=October 1, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141001034403/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000403246/article/raiders-fire-dennis-allen-after-twoplus-seasons|url-status=live}}</ref> Allen joined the staff of the New Orleans Saints for the 2015 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/01/20/dennis-allen-joins-saints-staff/|title=Dennis Allen joins Saints' staff|last=Smith|first=Michael D.|publisher=NBC Sports|date=January 20, 2015|website=profootballtalk.nbcsports.com|access-date=April 24, 2015|archive-date=August 18, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190818182825/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/01/20/dennis-allen-joins-saints-staff/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Sparano, formerly head coach of the Miami Dolphins, finished the season as interim head coach, compiling a record of 3–9.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Hanzus|first1=Dan|title=Tony Sparano named Raiders' interim head coach|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/tony-sparano-named-raiders-interim-head-coach-0ap3000000403464|work=NFL.com|access-date=30 September 2014|archive-date=October 3, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141003153927/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000403464/article/tony-sparano-to-be-raiders-interim-head-coach|url-status=live}}</ref> He then became tight ends coach for the San Francisco 49ers.<ref>{{cite news|title=Tony Sparano new 49ers TE coach|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/12211782/tony-sparano-joins-san-francisco-49ers-staff-tight-ends-coach|publisher=ESPN|date=22 January 2015|archive-date=November 30, 2024|access-date=July 17, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241130155417/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/12211782/tony-sparano-joins-san-francisco-49ers-staff-tight-ends-coach|url-status=live}}</ref>

Jack Del Rio was hired on January 14, 2015, to become their head coach after serving as defensive coordinator for Denver Broncos since 2012; he previously served as head coach of the Jacksonville Jaguars from 2003 to 2011.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Orr|first1=Conor|title=Oakland Raiders hire Jack Del Rio as next head coach|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/oakland-raiders-announce-jack-del-rio-as-new-coach-0ap3000000458717|website=NFL.com|access-date=14 January 2015|archive-date=February 27, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240227100141/https://www.nfl.com/news/oakland-raiders-announce-jack-del-rio-as-new-coach-0ap3000000458717|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
|style="text-align:center;"|[[San Francisco 49ers]]
|style="text-align:center;" colspan=2|[[Jim Harbaugh]]
|style="text-align:center;"|Mutually Part Ways
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Jim Tomsula]]
|Harbaugh compiled a record of 49–22–1 (.688), including postseason games, in four seasons with the 49ers, and led the team to three [[NFC Championship Game]] appearances and a berth in [[Super Bowl XLVII]]. After a mediocre 8–8 season in 2014 (the first time his team did not make the playoffs) and amid tensions between Harbaugh and the 49ers front office, Harbaugh left to become head coach at his college alma mater, the [[Michigan Wolverines football|University of Michigan]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Rosenthal|first1=Gregg|title=Jim Harbaugh, San Francisco 49ers mutually part ways|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/jim-harbaugh-san-francisco-49ers-mutually-part-ways-0ap3000000450865|work=NFL.com|access-date=29 September 2014|archive-date=April 13, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240413080457/https://www.nfl.com/news/jim-harbaugh-san-francisco-49ers-mutually-part-ways-0ap3000000450865|url-status=live}}</ref>

On January 14, 2015, Jim Tomsula was promoted to head coach after serving as defensive line coach with the team since 2007; it is his second time at the helm, as he previously served as the 49ers' interim head coach for one game, after [[Mike Singletary]]'s firing in 2010.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Patra|first1=Kevin|title=Niners choose to promote Jim Tomsula to head coach|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/niners-choose-to-promote-jim-tomsula-to-head-coach-0ap3000000458952|website=NFL.cpm|access-date=14 January 2015|archive-date=May 20, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240520125305/https://www.nfl.com/news/niners-choose-to-promote-jim-tomsula-to-head-coach-0ap3000000458952|url-status=live}}</ref>
|}

| rowspan="3" style="text-align:center;" |Fired
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Dan Campbell]]
|Philbin compiled a record of 24–28 ({{winning percentage|24|28}}), with no playoff appearances, in 3¼ seasons as head coach of the Dolphins. The Dolphins were expected to be contenders for a playoff position in 2015 but grossly underachieved, starting the season 1–3, which led to Philbin's firing. Campbell, the team's tight ends coach, took over for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/13814560/miami-dolphins-fire-joe-philbin|title=Dolphins fire coach Joe Philbin after team stumbles to 1-3 start|last=Walker|first=James|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=October 5, 2015|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 5, 2015|archive-date=January 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160125063747/http://espn.go.com/nfl/story/_/id/13814560/miami-dolphins-fire-joe-philbin|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Tennessee Titans]]
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Ken Whisenhunt]]
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Mike Mularkey]]
|Whisenhunt compiled a record of 3–20 ({{winning percentage|3|20}}), with no playoff appearances, in 1½ seasons as head coach of the Titans. After an impressive opening day win, the Titans lost six straight, resulting in Whisenhunt's dismissal. Mularkey, the team's tight ends coach, took over as interim head coach. Mularkey's previous head coaching experience includes two seasons with the Buffalo Bills (2004–05) and one season with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2012).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/tennessee-titans-fire-head-coach-ken-whisenhunt-0ap3000000572205|title=Tennessee Titans fire head coach Ken Whisenhunt|last=Orr|first=Conor|work=[[NFL.com]]|date=November 3, 2015|access-date=November 3, 2015|archive-date=January 6, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160106164651/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000572205/article/whisenhunt-relieved-of-duties-as-titans-head-coach|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Philadelphia Eagles]]
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Chip Kelly]]
|style="text-align:center;"|[[Pat Shurmur]]
|Kelly compiled a record of 26–21 ({{winning percentage|26|21}}) in almost three years with the Eagles. He led the team to the playoffs in 2013, but lost in the Wild Card. He was fired from both his head coach and ''de facto'' general manager positions when the team, after its ninth loss of the season, was eliminated from postseason contention with one game remaining on the schedule. Shurmur, the Eagles' offensive coordinator, filled in as head coach for the team's last game; he previously coached the Cleveland Browns from 2011 to 2012.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Rosenthal|first1=Gregg|title=Philadelphia Eagles fire coach Chip Kelly|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/philadelphia-eagles-fire-coach-chip-kelly-0ap3000000612168|website=NFL.com|access-date=30 December 2015|archive-date=January 1, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160101205114/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000612168/article/philadelphia-eagles-let-go-of-chip-kelly|url-status=live}}</ref>
|}

On January 13, 2015, the Jets hired Maccagnan as new general manager of the team. He was the director of college scouting for the Houston Texans prior to his hiring.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Hanzus|first1=Dan|title=Mike Maccagnan named new general manager of Jets|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/mike-maccagnan-named-new-general-manager-of-jets-0ap3000000458458|website=NFL.com|access-date=14 January 2015|archive-date=June 17, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240617044433/https://www.nfl.com/news/mike-maccagnan-named-new-general-manager-of-jets-0ap3000000458458|url-status=live}}</ref>

| style="text-align:center;"| [[Ryan Pace]] 
| Emery was fired after three seasons in Chicago.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bears fire general manager Phil Emery|website=[[NFL.com]]|url=http://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-am/0ap3000000451251/Bears-fire-general-manager-Phil-Emery|access-date=9 January 2015|archive-date=January 9, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150109123709/http://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-am/0ap3000000451251/Bears-fire-general-manager-Phil-Emery|url-status=live}}</ref>

Pace was hired on January 8, 2015, after serving as the director of player personnel with the Saints since 2013.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Biggs|first1=Brad|last2=Campbell|first2=Rich|last3=Wiederer|first3=Dan|title=Bears hire Ryan Pace as general manager|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/football/bears/chi-bears-hire-ryan-pace-gm-story.html|newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]]|access-date=8 January 2015|archive-date=January 9, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150109005708/http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/football/bears/chi-bears-hire-ryan-pace-gm-story.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

| style="text-align:center;"| [[General manager (American football)|GM]]
| style="text-align:center;"| [[Bruce Allen (American football)|Bruce Allen]]
| style="text-align:center;"| Replaced
| style="text-align:center;"| [[Scot McCloughan]]
| Bruce Allen was hired as general manager in December 2009 and was given the title of team president in May 2014.

Allen abdicated his title of general manager when McCloughan was hired as the new general manager of the team on January 7, 2015. The former 49ers general manager and Seahawks personnel executive will report to team president Bruce Allen and will have final say over the 53-man roster in D.C.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Orr|first1=Conor|title=Washington Redskins make Scot McCloughan GM|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/washington-redskins-make-scot-mccloughan-gm-0ap3000000454845|website=[[NFL.com]]|access-date=January 7, 2015|archive-date=January 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150108002100/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000454845/article/washington-redskins-make-scot-mccloughan-gm|url-status=live}}</ref>

| style="text-align:center;"|Fired
| style="text-align:center;"| [[Howie Roseman]]
| Roseman, who served as General Manager of the Eagles from 2010 to 2014, was promoted up to Executive Vice President of Football Operations. The General Manager position Roseman leaves behind remained unfilled, and head coach [[Chip Kelly]] fulfilled the duties of that position until his Week 16 firing.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gowton|first=Brandon|title=Eagles promote Howie Roseman; allow Chip Kelly to run player personnel department|url=http://www.bleedinggreennation.com/2015/1/2/7483051/eagles-promote-howie-roseman-chip-kelly-player-personnel-lurie|website=BleedingGreenNation.com|publisher=[[Vox Media, Inc.]]|access-date=December 2, 2015|date=January 2, 2015|archive-date=December 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208065514/http://www.bleedinggreennation.com/2015/1/2/7483051/eagles-promote-howie-roseman-chip-kelly-player-personnel-lurie|url-status=live}}</ref>

* On April 22, 2015, the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] fired head coach [[Scott Brooks]] after seven years with the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brooks out as Thunder coach after seven seasons|url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/04/22/oklahoma-city-thunder-fire-coach-scott-brooks.ap/index.html|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|date=April 22, 2015|access-date=April 22, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150920184351/http://www.nba.com/2015/news/04/22/oklahoma-city-thunder-fire-coach-scott-brooks.ap/index.html|archive-date=September 20, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* On April 30, 2015, the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] hired [[Billy Donovan]] as head coach.<ref>{{cite web |date=April 30, 2015 |title=Florida's Donovan named next coach of Thunder |url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/04/30/oklahoma-city-thunder-reach-deal-with-billy-donovan-as-coach.ap/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151022214414/http://www.nba.com/2015/news/04/30/oklahoma-city-thunder-reach-deal-with-billy-donovan-as-coach.ap/index.html |archive-date=October 22, 2015 |access-date=April 30, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>
* On May 12, 2015, the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] fired head coach [[Monty Williams]] after five years with the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelicans fire coach Williams after five seasons|url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/05/12/pelicans-fire-coach-monty-williams.ap/index.html|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|date=May 12, 2015|access-date=May 12, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150920184359/http://www.nba.com/2015/news/05/12/pelicans-fire-coach-monty-williams.ap/index.html|archive-date=September 20, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* On May 28, 2015, the [[Chicago Bulls]] fired head coach [[Tom Thibodeau]] after five years with the team.<ref>{{cite web |last=Seligman |first=Andrew |date=May 28, 2015 |title=Bulls fire coach Thibodeau after five seasons |url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/05/28/bulls-fire-tom-thibodeau.ap/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151024111241/http://www.nba.com/2015/news/05/28/bulls-fire-tom-thibodeau.ap/index.html |archive-date=October 24, 2015 |access-date=May 28, 2015 |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc}}</ref>
* On May 29, 2015, the [[Orlando Magic]] hired [[Scott Skiles]] as head coach.<ref>{{cite web |last=Savage |first=Dan |date=May 29, 2015 |title=Orlando Magic name Scott Skiles head coach |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-name-scott-skiles-head-coach |access-date=November 6, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>
* On May 30, 2015, the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] hired [[Alvin Gentry]] as head coach.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/new-orleans-pelicans-name-alvin-gentry-head-coach|title=New Orleans Pelicans Name Alvin Gentry Head Coach|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=May 30, 2015|access-date=May 30, 2015}}</ref>
* On June 2, 2015, the [[Chicago Bulls]] hired [[Fred Hoiberg]] as head coach.<ref>{{cite web |date=June 2, 2015 |title=Bulls name Fred Hoiberg head coach |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/release/bulls-name-hoiberg-head-coach |access-date=November 6, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>
* On June 15, 2015, the [[Denver Nuggets]] hired [[Michael Malone]] as head coach.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nuggets name Michael Malone new head coach|url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/06/15/nuggets-name-michael-malone-release/index.html|website=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|date=June 15, 2015|access-date=June 15, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151025202637/http://www.nba.com/2015/news/06/15/nuggets-name-michael-malone-release/index.html|archive-date=October 25, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* On September 10, 2015, the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] announced that assistant coach [[Sam Mitchell (basketball)|Sam Mitchell]] would take on the interim head coach role while [[Flip Saunders]] battled [[Hodgkin's lymphoma]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13625530 |title=Sam Mitchell serving as Wolves interim coach |work=ESPN.com |date=September 10, 2015 |access-date=November 23, 2015}}</ref> Saunders died on October 25, thus making Mitchell the new, full-term head coach for the season afterwards.<ref name="saunders">{{cite web |date=October 25, 2015 |title=Timberwolves President of Basketball Operations and Head Coach Phil "Flip" Saunders Passes Away |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-president-basketball-operations-and-head-coach-phil-flip-saunders-passes-away |access-date=November 6, 2023 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>
* On October 1, 2015, the [[Golden State Warriors]] announced that assistant coach [[Luke Walton]] would take on the interim head coach role while [[Steve Kerr]] recovers from back pain issues that he had throughout the summer.<ref>{{cite web |date=October 1, 2015 |title=Warriors Head Coach Steve Kerr to Take a Leave of Absence to Focus on Back Rehab |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/kerr-leave-of-absence-20151001 |access-date=November 6, 2023 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

====In-season====
*On November 18, 2015, the [[Houston Rockets]] fired head coach [[Kevin McHale (basketball)|Kevin McHale]] after five years with the team. Their assistant coach [[J. B. Bickerstaff]] would take on the interim head coach.<ref>{{cite web |date=November 18, 2015 |author1=Calvin Watkins |author2=Michael C. Wright |author3=Marc Stein |agency=AP |title=Rockets fire coach Kevin McHale |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/14160559 |access-date=November 6, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>
* On December 23, 2015, the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] announced that assistant coach [[Joe Prunty]] would take on the interim head coach role while [[Jason Kidd]] recovers after taking an indefinite leave to have hip surgery.<ref>{{cite web |date=December 20, 2015 |title=Bucks coach Kidd out indefinitely for hip surgery |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2015/12/20/bucks-coach-kidd-out-indefinitely-for-hip-surgery/77681312 |access-date=November 6, 2023 |work=USAToday.com}}</ref>
* On January 10, 2016, the [[Brooklyn Nets]] fired head coach [[Lionel Hollins]] after two years with the team. Assistant coach [[Tony Brown (basketball)|Tony Brown]] was named as interim head coach.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 10, 2016 |title=Nets Part Ways With Head Coach Lionel Hollins |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2016/01/10/nets-part-ways-with-head-coach-lionel-hollins |access-date=November 6, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>
* On January 22, 2016, [[Golden State Warriors]] coach [[Steve Kerr]] returned after complications following back surgery, taking over from [[Luke Walton]], who led the Warriors to a 39–4 record. Walton returns as an assistant coach for Kerr.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 22, 2016 |title=Warriors Head Coach Steve Kerr Makes Return to the Bench Tonight |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/kerr-returns-to-bench-20160122 |access-date=November 6, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>
* On January 22, 2016, the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] fired head coach [[David Blatt]] after one-and-a-half seasons with the team. Assistant coach [[Tyronn Lue]] was named the new head coach after signing a three-year deal with the Cavaliers.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 23, 2016 |author1=Dave McMenamin |author2=Ian Begley |agency=AP |title=David Blatt fired as Cavaliers coach; Tyronn Lue to take over team |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/14627529 |access-date=November 6, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>
* On January 26, 2016, [[Milwaukee Bucks]] coach [[Jason Kidd]] returned after complications following right hip surgery taking over from [[Joe Prunty]] who led the Bucks to an 8–9 record.<ref>{{cite web |last=Armasap |first=Genaro C. |date=January 25, 2016 |title=Bucks welcoming coach Jason Kidd back from hip surgery |url=https://apnews.com/article/731b1419e62049579a0aea600ad89069 |access-date=November 6, 2023 |website=apnews.com}}</ref>
* On February 1, 2016, the [[Phoenix Suns]] fired head coach [[Jeff Hornacek]] after two and a half seasons with the team. Suns' assistant coach [[Earl Watson]] was named as interim head coach.<ref>{{cite web|last=Baum|first=Bob|title=Reeling Suns fire coach Hornacek after 2½ seasons|url=http://www.nba.com/2016/news/02/01/suns-fire-jeff-hornacek.ap/index.html|work=NBA.com|date=February 1, 2016|access-date=February 1, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Ramirez |first=M. Y. |date=February 1, 2016 |title=Suns Name Earl Watson Interim Head Coach |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/suns-name-earl-watson-interim-head-coach |access-date=November 6, 2023 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> On April 19, the Suns decided to promote Watson as their full-time coach for the next three years.
* On February 8, 2016, the [[New York Knicks]] fired head coach [[Derek Fisher]] after one-and-a-half seasons with the team. Knicks assistant coach [[Kurt Rambis]] was named interim head coach for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web |date=February 8, 2016 |title=Knicks Relieve Fisher Coaching Duties |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-relieve-fisher-coaching-duties |access-date=November 6, 2023 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

|Pettine compiled a record of 10–22 ({{winning percentage|10|22}}) in two years with the Browns, finishing in last place in the AFC North both years. After putting up a promising record of 7–9 the season before, the team, marred by the actions of [[Johnny Manziel]] off the field, regressed heavily, forcing the Browns to hire their fifth head coach in eight seasons. The decision to fire Pettine came the day before the end of the regular season.<ref name="Brownsfired">{{cite web|last=Rosenthal|first=Gregg|title=Cleveland Browns fire Mike Pettine, GM Ray Farmer|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/cleveland-browns-fire-mike-pettine-gm-ray-farmer-0ap3000000614532|website=NFL.com|date=January 3, 2016|access-date=January 3, 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160104012019/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000614532/article/browns-gm-ray-farmer-out-in-cleveland|archive-date=January 4, 2016|df=mdy-all}}</ref>
On January 13, the Browns hired Jackson as their head coach. Jackson spent most of the past two seasons as the offensive coordinator for the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] and had previously served as head coach for the [[Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Wesseling|first1=Chris|title=Cleveland Browns hire Hue Jackson as head coach|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/cleveland-browns-hire-hue-jackson-as-head-coach-0ap3000000621189|website=NFL.com|access-date=13 January 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160116091451/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000621189/article/cleveland-browns-hire-hue-jackson-as-head-coach|archive-date=January 16, 2016|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

|Philbin compiled a record of 24–28 ({{winning percentage|24|28}}), with no playoff appearances, in 3¼ seasons as head coach of the Dolphins. The Dolphins were expected to be contenders for a playoff position in 2015 but grossly underachieved, starting the season 1–3, which led to Philbin's firing. Philbin joined the [[Indianapolis Colts]] as offensive line coach for 2016. Campbell, the team's tight ends coach, took over for the rest of the season; following the season, he joined the [[New Orleans Saints]] as tight ends coach.<ref>{{cite web|last=Walker|first=James|title=Dolphins fire coach Joe Philbin after team stumbles to 1–3 start|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/13814560/miami-dolphins-fire-joe-philbin|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=December 29, 2015|date=October 5, 2015|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160125063747/http://espn.go.com/nfl/story/_/id/13814560/miami-dolphins-fire-joe-philbin|archive-date=January 25, 2016|df=mdy-all}}</ref>
On January 9, the Dolphins hired Gase as their head coach. Gase had spent the past season as the offensive coordinator for the [[Chicago Bears]]; at age 37, Gase became the youngest active head coach in the NFL.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Sessler|first1=Marc|title=Miami Dolphins hire Adam Gase as new head coach|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/miami-dolphins-hire-adam-gase-as-new-head-coach-0ap3000000619758|website=NFL.com|access-date=10 January 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109215650/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000619758/article/miami-dolphins-hire-adam-gase-as-new-head-coach|archive-date=January 9, 2016|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

|Kelly was released on December 29, 2015, one week prior to the end of the regular season, following the Eagles being eliminated from playoff contention. He finished with a record of 26–21 ({{winning percentage|26|21}}) and one playoff appearance (a single loss in 2013) over almost three seasons. Heading into 2015, Kelly made several controversial roster moves as general manager that didn't pan out, leading to his firing. Offensive Coordinator (and former [[Cleveland Browns]] head coach) Pat Shurmur served as interim replacement for week 17.<ref name="Eaglesfired">{{cite web|last=Rosenthal|first=Gregg|title=Chip Kelly released by Philadelphia Eagles|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/philadelphia-eagles-fire-coach-chip-kelly-0ap3000000612168|website=NFL.com|access-date=2015-12-30|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160101205114/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000612168/article/philadelphia-eagles-let-go-of-chip-kelly|archive-date=January 1, 2016|df=mdy-all}}</ref> Shurmur finished 1–0 as the Eagles head coach, and was a frontrunner in the Eagles head coaching race along with [[Tom Coughlin]] and [[Doug Pederson]]; following the season, he joined the [[Minnesota Vikings]] as tight ends coach and later offensive coordinator after the sudden resignation of [[Norv Turner]].
On January 18, the Eagles hired Pederson as their head coach. Pederson had spent the previous three season as offensive coordinator for the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], and also was a former QB for the Eagles.<ref>{{cite web|last=Wesseling|first=Chris|title=Philadelphia Eagles hire Doug Pederson as coach|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/philadelphia-eagles-hire-doug-pederson-as-coach-0ap3000000622612|website=NFL.com|access-date=January 18, 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160120142223/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000622612/article/philadelphia-eagles-hire-doug-pederson-as-coach|archive-date=January 20, 2016|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

|Smith compiled a record of 8–24 ({{winning percentage|8|24}}), with no playoff appearances, in two years with the Buccaneers, finishing in last place in the NFC South both years.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Wesseling|first1=Chris|title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers fire Lovie Smith|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/tampa-bay-buccaneers-fire-lovie-smith-0ap3000000618589|website=NFL.com|date=January 6, 2016|access-date=January 6, 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160107083057/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000618589/article/tampa-bay-buccaneers-fire-lovie-smith|archive-date=January 7, 2016|df=mdy-all}}</ref> Smith moved to the college ranks, becoming the head coach of the university of [[Illinois Fighting Illini football]] team.
On January 14, Koetter was promoted to head coach after serving as offensive coordinator with the team since 2015.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Hanzus|first1=Dan|title=Buccaneers promote OC Dirk Koetter to head coach|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/buccaneers-promote-oc-dirk-koetter-to-head-coach-0ap3000000622328|website=NFL.com|date=January 14, 2016|access-date=January 14, 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160116102233/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000622328/article/buccaneers-promote-oc-dirk-koetter-to-head-coach|archive-date=January 16, 2016|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

| style="text-align:center;" colspan=2 |[[Mike Mularkey]]
|Whisenhunt compiled a record of 3–20 ({{winning percentage|3|20}}), with no playoff appearances, in 1½ seasons as head coach of the Titans. After an impressive opening day win, the Titans lost six straight, resulting in Whisenhunt's dismissal. Mularkey, the team's tight ends coach, took over as interim head coach.  Mularkey's previous head coaching experience includes two seasons with the [[Buffalo Bills]] (2004–05) and one season with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] (2012).<ref>{{cite web|last1=Orr|first1=Conor|title=Tennessee Titans fire head coach Ken Whisenhunt|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/tennessee-titans-fire-head-coach-ken-whisenhunt-0ap3000000572205|website=NFL.com|access-date=2015-12-29|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160106164651/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000572205/article/whisenhunt-relieved-of-duties-as-titans-head-coach|archive-date=January 6, 2016|df=mdy-all}}</ref> For 2016, Whisenhunt joined the [[San Diego Chargers]] as offensive coordinator.
On January 16, Mularkey shed the interim tag and was hired as the full-time head coach.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Sessler|first1=Marc|title=Mike Mularkey sheds interim tag, named Titans coach|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/mike-mularkey-sheds-interim-tag-named-titans-coach-0ap3000000623006|website=NFL.com|access-date=17 January 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160117175744/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000623006/article/mike-mularkey-sheds-interim-tag-named-titans-coach|archive-date=January 17, 2016|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

| style="text-align:center;" |Resigned
|Coughlin compiled a record of 102–90 ({{winning percentage|102|90}}) in 12 years with the Giants, a tenure that included three division titles, five playoff appearances (with a collective record of 8–3 in those games), and two Super Bowl wins ([[Super Bowl XLII]] and [[Super Bowl XLVI]], both over the [[New England Patriots]]). ====In-season====
There were no head coaching changes during the regular season. This was the first time since the [[1963–64 NBA season]] that there was no in-season coaching changes, the fourth time this happened in league history.<ref>{{cite news|title=An NBA first: Every coach who started last season is back|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2017/09/21/an-nba-first-every-coach-who-started-last-season-is-back/105857732/|newspaper=USA Today|date=September 21, 2017|access-date=September 21, 2017}}</ref>

He guided them to the division title in 2014 before losing to the San Francisco Giants. He finished with a 179–145 record.{{cite web |last=Gleeman |first=Aaron |date=October 5, 2015 |title=Nationals fire reigning manager of the year Matt Williams |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/mlb/news/nationals-fire-reigning-manager-of-the-year-matt-williams |access-date=2024-10-15 |website=NBC Sports}} On November 3, 2015, the Nationals announced that Dusty Baker will be their new manager for the 2016 season.{{cite web |last=Calcaterra |first=Craig |date=November 3, 2015 |title=It's Official Dusty Baker is the new Nationals Manager |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/mlb/news/its-official-dusty-baker-is-the-new-nationals-manager |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304050358/http://mlb.nbcsports.com/2015/11/03/it%27s-official-dusty-baker-is-the-new-nationals-manager/ |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |access-date=2024-10-15 |website=NBC Sports}} |- !scope="row"|[[San Diego Padres]] | style="text-align:center;"| [[Bud Black]] | style="text-align:center;"| [[Pat Murphy (baseball coach)|Pat Murphy]] | style="text-align:center;"| Fired | Style="text-align:center;"| [[Andy Green (baseball)|Andy Green]] | Pat Murphy was named interim manager on June 16, 2015, after Bud Black was fired. He finished the 2015 season with a record of 42–53.{{cite web |last=Baer |first=Bill |date=2015-10-04 |title=Padres announce that Pat Murphy won't return as manager in 2016 |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/mlb/news/padres-announce-pat-murphy-wont-return-as-manager-in-2016 |access-date=2024-10-15 |website=NBC Sports}} On October 29, 2015, Andy Green was named the new permanent manager of the Padres.{{cite web|last=Gleeman|first=Aaron|url=http://mlb.nbcsports.com/2015/10/29/padres-hire-diamondbacks-third-base-coach-andy-green-as-new-manager/|title=Padres hire Diamondbacks third base coach Andy Green as new manager|date=October 29, 2015|publisher=NBC Sports|access-date=October 29, 2015|archive-date=October 30, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151030014831/http://mlb.nbcsports.com/2015/10/29/padres-hire-diamondbacks-third-base-coach-andy-green-as-new-manager/|url-status=live}} |- !scope="row"|[[Miami Marlins]] | style="text-align:center;"| [[Mike Redmond]] | style="text-align:center;"| [[Dan Jennings (manager)|Dan Jennings]] | style="text-align:center;"| Fired | Style="text-align:center;"| [[Don Mattingly]] | Jennings made the unusual move from GM to manager when the Marlins fired Mike Redmond in May after a 16–22 start. The change failed to spark a turnaround, and the injury-riddled Marlins finished at 71–91, their sixth consecutive losing season. Jennings returned as GM{{cite web|url=http://mlb.nbcsports.com/10/06/15/dan-jennings-asked-to-return-as-the-marlins-gm/|title=Dan Jennings asked to return as the Marlins GM|last=Calcaterra|first=Craig|date=October 6, 2015|publisher=NBC Sports|access-date=October 6, 2015}} and was subsequently fired from that role. On October 29, 2015, Don Mattingly was named the new manager.{{cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/source-marlins-hire-don-mattingly-as-manager/|title=Source: Marlins Hire Don Mattingly as Manager|first=Molly|last=Knight|date=October 29, 2015|access-date=October 29, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151029231640/https://sports.vice.com/en_us/article/source-marlins-hire-don-mattingly-as-manager|archive-date=October 29, 2015|url-status=live}} |- !scope="row"|[[Seattle Mariners]] | style="text-align:center;"| [[Lloyd McClendon]] | style="text-align:center;"| None | style="text-align:center;"| Fired | Style="text-align:center;"| [[Scott Servais]] | McClendon compiled records of 87–75 in 2014 and 76–86 in 2015. On October 9, 2015, it was reported that new Mariners GM Jerry Dipoto wished to hire a new manager, rather than retain McClendon from the previous GM, Jack Zduriencik.{{cite web |last=Gleeman |first=Aaron |date=2015-10-09 |title=Mariners fire Lloyd McClendon |url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/mlb/mariners-fire-lloyd-mcclendon-after-two-seasons/1279329/ |access-date=2024-10-15 |website=NBC Sports}} On October 23, 2015, Scott Servais was the hired as the team's new manager.{{cite web |last=Gleeman |first=Aaron |date=October 22, 2015 |title=Scott Servais is the "strong frontrunner" to be Mariners' new manager |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/mlb/news/scott-servais-is-the-strong-frontrunner-to-be-mariners-new-manager |access-date=2024-10-15 |website=[[NBC Sports]] |archive-date=December 1, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241201184119/https://www.nbcsports.com/mlb/news/scott-servais-is-the-strong-frontrunner-to-be-mariners-new-manager |url-status=live }} |- !scope="row"|[[Los Angeles Dodgers]] | style="text-align:center;"| [[Don Mattingly]] | style="text-align:center;"| None | style="text-align:center;"| Mutual Decision | Style="text-align:center;"| [[Dave Roberts (outfielder)|Dave Roberts]] |Don Mattingly and the Dodgers parted ways on October 22 after five seasons together. The Dodgers had won their third straight NL West Championship, marking the first time in franchise history that they made the playoffs three years in a row. Their season ended when they lost to the New York Mets in the Division Series. Mattingly finished with a 446–363 record.{{cite web|last=Calcaterra|first=Craig|title=The Dodgers, Don Mattingly part ways|url=http://mlb.nbcsports.com/2015/10/22/the-dodgers-fire-don-mattingly/|website=hardballtalk.nbcsports.com|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|access-date=October 22, 2015|date=October 22, 2015|archive-date=October 22, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151022134921/http://mlb.nbcsports.com/2015/10/22/the-dodgers-fire-don-mattingly/|url-status=live}} On November 23, 2015, Dave Roberts was named the Los Angeles Dodgers new manager.{{cite web|last=Gurnick|first=Ken|title=Roberts is Dodgers' pick to be manager|url=https://www.mlb.com/dodgers/news/dave-roberts-named-dodgers-manager/c-157933286|website=[[MLB]].com|publisher=[[Major League Baseball Advanced Media|MLB Advanced Media, L.P.]]|access-date=February 1, 2020|location=[[Los Angeles]]|date=November 23, 2015|archive-date=February 1, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200201131740/https://www.mlb.com/dodgers/news/dave-roberts-named-dodgers-manager/c-157933286|url-status=live}} |} ====In-season==== {|class="wikitable plainrowheaders" align="center;" |- !scope="col"|Date !scope="col"|Team !scope="col"|Former manager !scope="col"|Interim manager !scope="col"|Reason for leaving !scope="col"|New manager !scope="col"|Notes |- | May 17 !scope="row"|[[Atlanta Braves]] | style="text-align:center;"|[[Fredi González]] | style="text-align:center;"|[[Brian Snitker]] | style="text-align:center;"|Fired | style="text-align:center;"|Brian Snitker | González was fired after starting the season with a 9–28 record, which was the worst record in baseball at the time. González in six-plus seasons finished with a 434–413 record with two playoff appearances.{{cite news|last=O'Brien|first=David|title=Braves fire Fredi Gonzalez as manager|url=http://www.ajc.com/news/sports/baseball/braves-fire-gonzalez-as-manager/nrN5k/|access-date=May 17, 2016|work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|publisher=[[Cox Enterprises]]|date=May 17, 2016|location=[[Pittsburgh]]|archive-date=May 18, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160518231510/http://www.ajc.com/news/sports/baseball/braves-fire-gonzalez-as-manager/nrN5k/|url-status=live}}{{cite web|last=Bowman|first=Mark|title=Gonzalez dismissed as manager of Braves|url=https://www.mlb.com/braves/news/braves-dismiss-fredi-gonzalez-c178615590|website=[[MLB]].com|publisher=[[Major League Baseball Advanced Media|MLB Advanced Media, L.P.]]|access-date=February 1, 2020|location=[[Pittsburgh]]|date=May 17, 2016|archive-date=February 1, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200201131648/https://www.mlb.com/braves/news/braves-dismiss-fredi-gonzalez-c178615590|url-status=live}}
After the season was over, Brian Snitker was named as the new manager on October 11, 2016, dropping the "interim" title.{{cite news|last=O'Brien|first=David|title=Brian Snitker named Braves' new manager|url=http://www.ajc.com/sports/baseball/brian-snitker-named-braves-new-manager/Q7p77X1UI0b4ZuBswqT9LJ/|access-date=October 11, 2016|work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|publisher=[[Cox Enterprises]]|date=October 11, 2016|archive-date=October 12, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161012150915/http://www.ajc.com/sports/baseball/brian-snitker-named-braves-new-manager/Q7p77X1UI0b4ZuBswqT9LJ/|url-status=live}} |}

|Brown was fired on December 7. Brown, who had served as the team's lawyer since 2013, was given the duties of general manager in 2016 despite no prior experience in football. ====Off-season====
For the first time since the inauguration of the [[Basketball Association of America|BAA]], there would be no coaching changes going from the previous season to entering the regular season.<ref>{{cite web|title=An NBA first: Every coach who started last season is back|url=http://nba.nbcsports.com/2017/09/22/an-nba-first-every-coach-who-started-last-season-is-back/|website=nbcsports.com|access-date=September 28, 2017|date=September 22, 2017}}</ref> In fact, the 536 days from [[Dave Joerger]] being fired as coach of the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] to the day the [[Phoenix Suns]] fired [[Earl Watson]] as head coach would be the longest period in NBA history without any coaching changes occur. The last time no head coaches were hired in the off-season occurred during the [[1975–76 NBA season|1975–76 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://static.nytimes.com/email-content/MSB_352.html?nlid=60638453 |title=Marc Stein |publisher=Static.nytimes.com |date=March 19, 2018 |accessdate=June 10, 2022}}</ref>

====In-season====
* On October 22, 2017, the [[Phoenix Suns]] fired head coach [[Earl Watson]] and replaced him with the team's associate coach [[Jay Triano]] as interim head coach for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Suns Relieve Earl Watson of Head Coaching Duties|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/suns-relieve-earl-watson-head-coaching-duties|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2017|access-date=October 22, 2017}}</ref>
* On November 27, 2017, the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] fired head coach [[David Fizdale]] and replaced him with the team's associate head coach [[J. B. Bickerstaff]], removing the interim tag after the season concluded.<ref>{{cite web|title=Grizzlies relieve David Fizdale of head coaching duties|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-relieve-david-fizdale-171126|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 27, 2017|date=November 27, 2017}}</ref>
* On January 22, 2018, the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] fired head coach [[Jason Kidd]] and replaced him with the team's assistant head coach [[Joe Prunty]] as interim head coach for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucks Relieve Jason Kidd Of Head Coaching Duties|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-relieve-jason-kidd-head-coaching-duties|website=Milwaukee Bucks|access-date=January 23, 2018|date=January 22, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Joe Prunty to remain head coach of Milwaukee Bucks for remainder of season|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/01/26/joe-prunty-remain-milwaukee-bucks-coach-official-release#/|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 26, 2018}}</ref>

On November 4, 2016, Torey Lovullo was hired as the new manager.{{cite web|last=Gilbert|first=Steve|title=D-backs introduce Lovullo as new manager|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/d-backs-name-torey-lovullo-manager-c208129626|website=[[MLB.com]]|publisher=[[MLB Advanced Media]]|access-date=November 8, 2016|location=[[Phoenix, Arizona]]|date=November 8, 2016|archive-date=October 20, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191020071203/https://www.mlb.com/news/d-backs-name-torey-lovullo-manager-c208129626|url-status=live}} |- | style="text-align:center;" |[[Atlanta Braves]] | style="text-align:center;" | [[Fredi González]] | style="text-align:center;" | [[Brian Snitker]] | On October 11, 2016, Brian Snitker was named as the new manager of the Atlanta Braves after completing the 2016 season as the interim manager.{{cite news|last=O'Brien|first=David|title=Brian Snitker named Braves' new manager|url=http://www.ajc.com/sports/baseball/brian-snitker-named-braves-new-manager/Q7p77X1UI0b4ZuBswqT9LJ/|access-date=October 11, 2016|work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|publisher=[[Cox Enterprises]]|date=October 11, 2016|archive-date=October 12, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161012150915/http://www.ajc.com/sports/baseball/brian-snitker-named-braves-new-manager/Q7p77X1UI0b4ZuBswqT9LJ/|url-status=live}} Snitker took over for [[Fredi González]] on May 17, 2016, and finished the season with a 59–65 record. |- | style="text-align:center;" |[[Chicago White Sox]] | style="text-align:center;" | [[Robin Ventura]] | rowspan=2 style="text-align:center;" | Resigned | style="text-align:center;" | [[Rick Renteria]] | At the conclusion of the 2016 regular season, Chicago White Sox manager [[Robin Ventura]] resigned.
On October 3, 2016, Rick Renteria became the team's new manager.{{cite news|last=Kane|first=Colleen|title=Robin Ventura leaving White Sox, says organization 'needs a new voice'|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/baseball/whitesox/ct-white-sox-robin-ventura-last-game-20161002-story.html|access-date=October 3, 2016|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|publisher=[[Tronc]]|date=October 2, 2016|archive-date=October 3, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161003062602/http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/baseball/whitesox/ct-white-sox-robin-ventura-last-game-20161002-story.html|url-status=live}} Ventura finished his five seasons in Chicago with a record of 375–435 with no playoff appearances. |- | style="text-align:center;" |[[Colorado Rockies]] | style="text-align:center;" | [[Walt Weiss]] | style="text-align:center;" | [[Bud Black]] | On October 3, 2016, Walt Weiss resigned as manager of the Colorado Rockies after four years without a winning record or a playoff appearance.{{cite news|last=Saunders|first=Patrick|title=Walt Weiss resigns as Colorado Rockies manager, citing poor working relationship with front office|url=http://www.denverpost.com/2016/10/03/walt-weiss-steps-down-colorado-rockies-manager/|access-date=October 3, 2016|work=[[The Denver Post]]|publisher=[[Digital First Media]]|date=October 3, 2016|archive-date=October 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161004162947/http://www.denverpost.com/2016/10/03/walt-weiss-steps-down-colorado-rockies-manager/|url-status=live}} Weiss finished with a 283–365 record during his tenure.
On November 6, 2016, the Rockies announced they were hiring Bud Black as manager.{{cite news|last1=Kosmider|first1=Nick|last2=Saunders|first2=Patrick|title=Bud Black reaches agreement with Colorado Rockies to become new manager|url=http://www.denverpost.com/2016/11/06/colorado-rockies-hire-bud-black-new-manager/|work=[[The Denver Post]]|publisher=[[Digital First Media]]|date=November 6, 2016|access-date=November 7, 2016|archive-date=November 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107221418/http://www.denverpost.com/2016/11/06/colorado-rockies-hire-bud-black-new-manager/|url-status=live}} |}

news|url=https://www.al.com/sports/2019/03/alabama-am-removes-interim-tag-from-mens-basketball-coach-dylan-howard.html|title=Alabama A&M removes interim tag from men's basketball coach Dylan Howard|newspaper=[[Birmingham News]]|first=Daniel|last=Boyette|date=March 19, 2019|access-date=March 20, 2019}} |- | [[Bryant Bulldogs men's basketball|Bryant]] | [[Tim O'Shea]] | | [[Jared Grasso]] | The 56-year-old O'Shea announced on February 12 that he would retire at the end of the season.{{cite press release|url=http://www.bryantbulldogs.com/sports/mbkb/2017-18/releases/20180211ndl4o8|title=Men's basketball head coach Tim O'Shea to announce retirement Monday afternoon|publisher=[[Bryant Bulldogs men's basketball|Bryant Bulldogs]]|date=February 11, 2018|access-date=February 12, 2018}} The Bulldogs went 96–210 during O'Shea's 10-year tenure, including a 3–28 overall record and 2–16 in conference play this season. On March 30, Iona associate head coach Grasso was hired by Bryant for the head coaching position.{{cite news|url=https://www.fanragsports.com/news/rothstein-bryant-to-hire-ionas-jared-grasso-as-next-hoops-coach/|title=Bryant to hire Iona's Jared Grasso as next hoops coach|website=fanragsports.com|first=Jon|last=Rothstein|date=March 30, 2018|access-date=March 31, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180401004946/https://www.fanragsports.com/news/rothstein-bryant-to-hire-ionas-jared-grasso-as-next-hoops-coach/|archive-date=April 1, 2018|url-status=dead}} |- | [[Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball|Cal State Northridge]] | [[Reggie Theus]] | | [[Mark Gottfried]] | Cal State Northridge parted ways with Theus on March 6 after five seasons, finishing with a 53–105 record with no postseason appearances.{{cite news |last1=Goodman |first1=Jeff |last2=Borzello |first2=Jeff |name-list-style=and |date=March 6, 2018 |title=Reggie Theus to exit as CSU Northridge coach, sources say |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22671296 |access-date=March 6, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}} Former North Carolina State head coach Gottfried was named head coach of the Matadors on March 13.{{cite news|url=http://www.latimes.com/la-sp-mark-gottfried-csun-20180312-story.html|title=Mark Gottfried to coach men's basketball at CSUN, and Jim Harrick could join him|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]|first=Eric|last=Sondheimer|date=March 12, 2018|access-date=March 12, 2018}} |- | [[Charlotte 49ers men's basketball|Charlotte]] | [[Mark Price]] | [[Houston Fancher]] | [[Ron Sanchez]] | Price was fired on December 14 after a 3–6 start and a 30–42 record overall in 2½ seasons at Charlotte. He was replaced on an interim basis by assistant Fancher for the rest of the season.{{cite news |last=Goodman |first=Jeff |date=December 14, 2017 |title=Charlotte dismisses coach Mark Price in third season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/21768006 |access-date=December 15, 2017 |website=ESPN.com}} Virginia associate head coach Sanchez was hired as head coach of the 49ers on March 19.{{cite news |last=Goodman |first=Jeff |date=March 19, 2018 |title=Charlotte hires Virginia assistant Ron Sanchez as head coach |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22835648 |access-date=March 19, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}} |- | [[Chicago State Cougars men's basketball|Chicago State]] | [[Tracy Dildy]] | | [[Lance Irvin]] |Chicago State fired Dildy on the week of March 5, although it was not officially confirmed until March 12. The Cougars struggled during Dildy's eight-year tenure, which saw them lose at least 20 games in seven of those seasons.{{cite news|url=https://chicagocrusader.com/chicago-state-fires-womens-and-mens-basketball-coaches/|title=Chicago State fires women's and men's basketball coaches|first=J. Coyden|last=Palmer|website=chicagocrusader.com|date=March 15, 2018|access-date=March 21, 2018}} After a nearly five-month search, including hiring [[Chris Zorich]] as the new athletic director, the school hired Lance Irvin, a Chicago native and former assistant coach at DePaul and several other schools, as the new head coach on August 7.{{cite news|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-chicago-state-hires-basketball-coaches-20180807-story.html|title=Chicago State hires new women's and men's basketball coaches|newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=August 7, 2018|access-date=August 9, 2018}} |- | [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]] | [[Larry Eustachy]] | [[Steve Barnes (basketball)|Steve Barnes]]
[[Jase Herl]] | [[Niko Medved]] | Eustachy, who was in his sixth season at Colorado State, was placed on administrative leave on February 3 amid an internal investigation into his conduct with players and staff members. He had previously been sanctioned by the university in 2017 for emotionally abusing players and assistant coaches from a university led investigation in 2014. Top assistant Steve Barnes was initially named as the interim replacement.{{cite news |date=February 3, 2018 |title=Larry Eustachy put on administrative leave by Colorado State amid conduct investigation |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22309514 |access-date=February 11, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}} A later report by ''[[The Denver Post]]'' indicated that school officials planned to fire Eustachy with cause, and were negotiating a contract buyout.{{cite news |last=Schlabach |first=Mark |author-link=Mark Schlabach |date=February 9, 2018 |title=Source: CSU officials don't intend for Larry Eustachy to return as coach |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22380790 |access-date=February 11, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}} On February 10, hours before the Rams' home game against [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Jose State]], the school placed Barnes on administrative leave after two games, and Barnes' top assistant Jase Herl was named interim coach for the rest of the season.{{cite news |date=February 11, 2018 |title=Interim coach Steve Barnes suspended before game; assistant Jase Herl guides Rams to victory |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22396751 |access-date=February 12, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}} On February 26, Eustachy resigned after reaching a buyout agreement.{{cite news |date=February 26, 2018 |title=Larry Eustachy steps down at Colorado State after being put on administrative leave |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22589155 |access-date=February 26, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}} On March 22, Drake head coach and former Colorado State assistant Medved was named the new head coach.{{cite news|url=http://www.reporterherald.com/sports/csu/ci_31753408/colorado-state-set-hire-niko-medved-its-mens|title=Colorado State set to hire Niko Medved as its men's basketball head coach|newspaper=[[Reporter-Herald]]|location=[[Loveland, Colorado|Loveland, CO]]|first=Sean|last=Star|date=March 22, 2018|access-date=March 22, 2018}} |- | [[Delaware State Hornets men's basketball|Delaware State]] | [[Keith Walker (basketball)|Keith Walker]] | [[Keith Johnson (basketball)|Keith Johnson]] | [[Eric Skeeters]] | Walker was fired on February 22 after five seasons at Delaware State, finishing with a 43–96 record, including a 3–25 record this season at the time of his firing. Associate head coach Johnson was named interim head coach of the Hornets for the rest of the season.{{cite web|url=https://hoopdirt.com/official-keith-walker-relieved-duties-head-basketball-coach-delaware-state/|title=OFFICIAL: Keith Walker Relieved of Duties as Head Basketball Coach at Delaware State|website=hoopdirt.com|date=February 22, 2018|access-date=February 23, 2018}} More than five months after Walker's firing, along with hiring a new athletic director, the school hired UMBC assistant coach Skeeters for the job on July 25.{{cite news|url=https://www.delawareonline.com/story/sports/college/2018/07/25/delaware-state-hires-umbc-aide-eric-skeeters-basketball-coach/838343002/|title=Delaware State hires UMBC aide Eric Skeeters as basketball coach|newspaper=[[The News Journal]]|location=[[Wilmington, Delaware|Wilmington, DE]]|first=Kevin|last=Tresolini|date=July 25, 2018|access-date=July 26, 2018}} |- | [[Detroit Titans men's basketball|Detroit]] | [[Bacari Alexander]] | | [[Mike Davis (basketball coach)|Mike Davis]] | Detroit fired Alexander on March 26 after two seasons at his alma mater, finishing 16–47 overall including a last place finish in Horizon league play this season.{{cite news|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2018/03/26/detroit-mercy-fires-bacari-alexander/459436002/|title=Bacari Alexander out as Detroit Mercy's basketball coach after 2 seasons|newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]]|first=Perry A.|last=Farrell|date=March 26, 2018|access-date=March 26, 2018}} The school hired Texas Southern's Mike Davis as the new head coach on June 13.{{cite news|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/2018/06/13/source-detroit-mercy-hires-mike-davis-presser-thursday/698750002/|title=Mike Davis hired by Detroit Mercy; Creighton assistant coach DeVries was named head coach of the Bulldogs on March 29.{{cite news|url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/drake/drake-bulldogs/2018/03/29/drake-hires-creighton-assistant-darian-devries-head-mens-basketball-coach/468525002/|title=Drake hires Creighton assistant Darian DeVries as head men's basketball coach|newspaper=[[Des Moines Register]]|first=Matthew|last=Bain|date=March 29, 2018|access-date=March 29, 2018}} |- | [[East Carolina Pirates men's basketball|East Carolina]] | [[Jeff Lebo]] | [[Michael Perry (basketball)|Michael Perry]] | [[Joe Dooley (basketball)|Joe Dooley]] | Lebo announced his resignation from ECU on November 29, 2017, after a 2–4 start to the season and a 116–122 overall record with no NCAA tournament appearances in eight seasons with the program. Assistant Michael Perry was named interim head coach of the Pirates for the rest of the season.{{cite news|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/aac/east-carolina-university/article187153283.html|title=Jeff Lebo out as East Carolina basketball coach|first=Steve|last=Wiseman|newspaper=[[The News & Observer]]|location=[[Raleigh, North Carolina|Raleigh, NC]]|date=November 29, 2017|access-date=November 29, 2017}} After the season was over, ECU brought back one of its former head coaches in Dooley, who had led the Pirates from 1995 to 1999, from Florida Gulf Coast on April 4.{{cite news |date=April 4, 2018 |title=East Carolina brings back Joe Dooley as head coach |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/23032046 |access-date=April 5, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}} |- | [[Eastern Kentucky Colonels men's basketball|Eastern Kentucky]] | [[Dan McHale]] | | [[A. In three seasons at EKU, he was 38–55 overall and 16–34 in OVC play, and failed to qualify for the OVC Tournament during his tenure at Eastern Kentucky.{{cite news |date=February 26, 2018 |title=Eastern Kentucky fires basketball coach Dan McHale after 3 seasons |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22586135 |access-date=February 26, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}} On March 23, EKU hired North Carolina State assistant Hamilton as the new head coach.{{cite news|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/nc-state/article206589414.html|title=NC State's AW Hamilton takes over men's basketball program at Eastern Kentucky|newspaper=The News & Observer|first=Aaron|last=Moody|date=March 23, 2018|access-date=March 25, 2018}} |- | [[Evansville Purple Aces men's basketball|Evansville]] | [[Marty Simmons]] | | [[Walter McCarty]] | Evansville fired Simmons on March 13 after 11 seasons. news |last1=Goodman |first1=Jeff |last2=Borzello |first2=Jeff |name-list-style=and |date=March 13, 2018 |title=Sources: Marty Simmons out after 11 seasons at Evansville The Flames made the playoffs in Gulutzan's first season with the team before missing out the following year.<ref>{{cite web|title=FLAMES RELIEVE THREE COACHES OF DUTIES|url=https://www.nhl.com/flames/news/flames-relieve-three-coaches-of-duties-298070934|website=NHL.com|access-date=April 18, 2018|date=April 17, 2018|archive-date=December 12, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241212010508/https://www.nhl.com/flames/news/flames-relieve-three-coaches-of-duties-298070934|url-status=live}}</ref> On April 23, Peters was named the Flames' new head coach.<ref>{{cite web|title=FLAMES NAME BILL PETERS HEAD COACH|url=https://www.nhl.com/flames/news/flames-name-bill-peters-head-coach-298204838|website=NHL.com|access-date=April 24, 2018|date=April 23, 2018|archive-date=January 19, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250119193357/https://www.nhl.com/flames/news/flames-name-bill-peters-head-coach-298204838|url-status=live}}</ref> He had coached the Carolina Hurricanes the previous four seasons.

| [[Carolina Hurricanes]]
| [[Bill Peters (ice hockey)|Bill Peters]]
| [[Rod Brind'Amour]]
| Peters resigned on April 20, following the Hurricanes' failure to make the playoffs. Under Peters the Hurricanes went 137–138–53 and missed the playoffs in all four seasons.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Terry|first1=Miles|title=Bill Peters Resigns Position as Head Coach|url=https://www.nhl.com/hurricanes/news/bill-peters-resigns-position-as-head-coach-298142812|website=NHL.com|access-date=April 20, 2018|date=April 20, 2018|archive-date=October 8, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231008191536/https://www.nhl.com/hurricanes/news/bill-peters-resigns-position-as-head-coach-298142812|url-status=live}}</ref> On May 8, Brind'Amour, who had spent the previous seven years as an assistant coach for the Hurricanes, was named the Hurricanes' new head coach.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Williams|first1=Terrell|title=Hurricanes Name Rod Brind'Amour as Head Coach|url=https://www.nhl.com/hurricanes/news/canes-name-rod-brindamour-as-head-coach-298520688|website=NHL.com|access-date=May 8, 2018|date=May 8, 2018|archive-date=November 13, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231113185141/https://www.nhl.com/hurricanes/news/canes-name-rod-brindamour-as-head-coach-298520688|url-status=live}}</ref>

| [[Dallas Stars]]
| [[Ken Hitchcock]]
| [[Jim Montgomery (ice hockey)|Jim Montgomery]]
| Hitchcock retired from coaching on April 13, following the Stars' failure to make the playoffs to become a consultant for the franchise. The Stars went 319–186–60–20 under Hitchcock, winning the [[Stanley Cup]] in [[1999 Stanley Cup Final|1999]], going back the following season, and winning the [[Presidents' Trophy]] twice.<ref>{{cite web|title=Stars head coach Ken Hitchcock announces retirement|url=https://www.nhl.com/stars/news/dallas-stars-head-coach-ken-hitchcock-announces-retirement-297955464|website=NHL.com|access-date=April 14, 2018|date=April 13, 2018|archive-date=April 13, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250413050012/https://www.nhl.com/stars/news/dallas-stars-head-coach-ken-hitchcock-announces-retirement-297955464|url-status=live}}</ref> On May 4, Montgomery was named the Stars' new head coach.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.star-telegram.com/sports/nhl/dallas-stars/article210458909.html |title=Dallas Stars dip into college ranks to get their new head coach |work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |date=May 4, 2018 |access-date=May 4, 2018 |archive-date=May 5, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180505065706/http://www.star-telegram.com/sports/nhl/dallas-stars/article210458909.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He previously coached the [[Denver Pioneers men's ice hockey|Denver Pioneers]] with whom he won the [[2017 NCAA Division I Men's Ice Hockey Tournament|2017 NCAA championship]].

| [[New York Islanders]]
| [[Doug Weight]]
| [[Barry Trotz]]
| Weight was relieved of his duties by the Islanders on June 5, a few weeks after the hiring of [[Lou Lamoriello]] as the president of hockey operations for the Islanders. The Islanders went 59–49–14 under Weight in his one-and-a-half seasons as head coach, never making the playoffs. Weight would remain with the Islanders.<ref name="ESPN">{{Cite web |url=http://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/23705606/new-york-islanders-fire-long-gm-garth-snow-head-coach-doug-weight |title=Islanders fire GM Garth Snow, head coach Doug Weight |work=[[ESPN]] |date=June 5, 2018 |access-date=June 5, 2018 |archive-date=June 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180608005042/http://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/23705606/new-york-islanders-fire-long-gm-garth-snow-head-coach-doug-weight |url-status=live }}</ref> On June 21, Trotz was hired as head coach, and was previously the head coach of the [[Nashville Predators]] and [[Washington Capitals]] with whom he won the [[Stanley Cup]] in [[2018 Stanley Cup Final|2018]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Trotz Named Head Coach |url=https://www.nhl.com/islanders/news/trotz-named-head-coach-299164546 |website=NHL.com |access-date=June 21, 2018 |date=June 21, 2018 |archive-date=December 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241204112253/https://www.nhl.com/islanders/news/trotz-named-head-coach-299164546 |url-status=live }}</ref>

| [[New York Rangers]]
| [[Alain Vigneault]]
| [[David Quinn (ice hockey)|David Quinn]]
| Vigneault was fired by the New York Rangers on April 7, hours after the team's last regular season game after failing to make the playoffs for the first time in nearly a decade and the second time since the [[2004–05 NHL lockout]]. The Rangers went 226–147–37 under Vigneault, going to the Final in his first year as head coach and winning the Presidents' Trophy the following season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/04/08/sports/hockey/alain-vigneault-fired-from-rangers/|title=Alain Vigneault Fired From Rangers|website=[[The New York Times]]|date=April 8, 2018|access-date=April 8, 2018}}</ref> On May 23, Quinn was named the Rangers' new head coach.<ref>{{cite web|title=David Quinn Named Rangers Head Coach|url=https://www.nhl.com/rangers/news/david-quinn-named-rangers-head-coach-298736554|website=NHL.com|access-date=May 23, 2018|date=May 23, 2018|archive-date=August 13, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250813024249/https://www.nhl.com/rangers/news/david-quinn-named-rangers-head-coach-298736554|url-status=live}}</ref> He previously served as the assistant coach for the [[Colorado Avalanche]] during the 2012–13 season.

| [[Washington Capitals]]
| [[Barry Trotz]]
| [[Todd Reirden]]
| Trotz resigned on June 18 amid speculation of a contract dispute that neither he nor the Capitals confirmed.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gulitti |first1=Tom |title=Trotz, Capitals will know his worth soon enough |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/barry-trotz-and-washington-capitals-will-soon-know-how-much-coach-is-w-299108864 |website=NHL.com |access-date=June 19, 2018 |date=June 18, 2018 |archive-date=January 19, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250119111504/https://www.nhl.com/news/barry-trotz-and-washington-capitals-will-soon-know-how-much-coach-is-w-299108864 |url-status=live }}</ref> In four seasons under Trotz, the Capitals went 205–89–34, won two Presidents' Trophies and won the [[2018 Stanley Cup Final]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gulitti |first1=Tom |title=Trotz leaves as coach of Capitals |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/barry-trotz-resigns-as-washington-capitals-coach-299101550 |website=NHL.com |access-date=June 19, 2018 |date=June 18, 2018 |archive-date=May 17, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240517223854/https://www.nhl.com/news/barry-trotz-resigns-as-washington-capitals-coach-299101550 |url-status=live }}</ref> On June 29, Reirden was named head coach by the Capitals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Capitals Name Todd Reirden Head Coach |url=https://www.nhl.com/capitals/news/capitals-name-todd-reirden-head-coach-299340814 |website=NHL.com |access-date=July 2, 2018 |date=June 29, 2018 |archive-date=June 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240604084737/https://www.nhl.com/capitals/news/capitals-name-todd-reirden-head-coach-299340814 |url-status=live }}</ref> Reirden, in his first NHL head coach position, had been an assistant with the Capitals for all four seasons under Trotz.

General manager Murray took over as interim head coach for the rest of the season.<ref name="CarlyleOut"/>

| [[Chicago Blackhawks]]
| [[Joel Quenneville]]
| [[Jeremy Colliton]]
| Quenneville was fired on November 6, 2018, after starting the season 6–6–3.<ref name="November 6">{{cite web |title=RELEASE: Blackhawks make coaching change |url=https://www.nhl.com/blackhawks/news/release-blackhawks-make-coaching-change-301652676 |website=NHL.com |access-date=November 6, 2018 |date=November 6, 2018 |archive-date=July 18, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240718150551/https://www.nhl.com/blackhawks/news/release-blackhawks-make-coaching-change-301652676 |url-status=live }}</ref> Quenneville had been the head coach of the team since 2008 and guided them to three [[Stanley Cup]]s in [[2010 Stanley Cup Final|2010]], [[2013 Stanley Cup Final|2013]] and [[2015 Stanley Cup Final|2015]], while also accumulating an overall record of 797–452–249 with the team. [[Jeremy Colliton]], the head coach for the [[Rockford IceHogs]], succeeded Quenneville as head coach of the Blackhawks.<ref name="November 6"/>
|-
| [[Edmonton Oilers]]
| [[Todd McLellan]]
| [[Ken Hitchcock]]*
| McLellan was fired on November 20, 2018, after starting the season 9–10–1.<ref name="McLellanOut">{{cite web |url=https://www.tsn.ca/oilers-fire-mclellan-hire-hitchcock-as-new-head-coach-1.1212882 |title=Oilers fire McLellan, hire Hitchcock as new head coach |website=TSN.ca |date=November 20, 2018 |access-date=November 20, 2018 |archive-date=November 20, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181120205334/https://www.tsn.ca/oilers-fire-mclellan-hire-hitchcock-as-new-head-coach-1.1212882 |url-status=live }}</ref> McLellan had been the Oilers' head coach since the 2015–16 season, leading the team to a 123–119–24 record and a playoff berth in 2016–17. Hitchcock, a head coach with the third most wins in the NHL, was hired out of his announced retirement to replace McLellan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=RELEASE: Oilers name Ken Hitchcock head coach |url=https://www.nhl.com/oilers/news/release-oilers-name-ken-hitchcock-head-coach-302127280 |website=NHL.com |access-date=November 21, 2018 |date=November 20, 2018 |archive-date=July 16, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240716151041/https://www.nhl.com/oilers/news/release-oilers-name-ken-hitchcock-head-coach-302127280 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://edmontonjournal.com/sports/hockey/nhl/cult-of-hockey/the-edmonton-oilers-fire-todd-mclellan-hire-hitch-as-they-try-to-stop-their-slide-in-a-hungry-shark-tank |title=The Edmonton Oilers fire Todd McLellan, hire Hitch as they try to stop their slide in a hungry Shark tank |work=The Edmonton Journal |date=November 20, 2018 |access-date=November 20, 2018 |archive-date=November 20, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181120222844/https://edmontonjournal.com/sports/hockey/nhl/cult-of-hockey/the-edmonton-oilers-fire-todd-mclellan-hire-hitch-as-they-try-to-stop-their-slide-in-a-hungry-shark-tank |url-status=live }}</ref>

| [[John Stevens (ice hockey)|John Stevens]]
| [[Willie Desjardins]]*
| Stevens was fired on November 4, 2018, after starting the season 4–8–1.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/john-stevens-fired-as-kings-coach-willie-desjardins-named-replacement-301612046 |title=Stevens fired as coach of Kings, Desjardins named replacement |website=NHL.com |date=November 4, 2018 |access-date=July 27, 2026 |archive-date=July 26, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260726040414/https://www.nhl.com/news/john-stevens-fired-as-kings-coach-willie-desjardins-named-replacement-301612046 |url-status=live }}</ref> Under his only season as head coach of the Kings, Stevens led the team to a 45–29–8 record and a wild card playoff berth in 2017–18. | [[Guy Boucher]]
| [[Marc Crawford]]*
| Boucher was fired on March 1, 2019, with the Senators having a 22–37–5 record and losing six consecutive games.<ref name="BoucherOut">{{cite web |title=Marc Crawford named interim head coach of rebuilding Ottawa Senators |url=https://www.nhl.com/senators/news/marc-crawford-named-interim-head-coach-of-rebuilding-ottawa-senators-305356826 |website=NHL.com |access-date=March 1, 2019 |date=March 1, 2019 |archive-date=December 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241207112349/https://www.nhl.com/senators/news/marc-crawford-named-interim-head-coach-of-rebuilding-ottawa-senators-305356826 |url-status=live }}</ref> Boucher had coached the Senators since the [[2016–17 NHL season|2016–17 season]] with a record of 94–108–26 and making it to the conference finals in 2017.
