| [[Dave Hakstol]]
| [[Scott Gordon (ice hockey)|Scott Gordon]]*
| Hakstol was fired on December 17, 2018, after starting the season 12–15–4.<ref>{{cite web |title=Flyers Relieve Dave Hakstol of Head Coaching Duties |url=https://www.nhl.com/flyers/news/flyers-relieve-dave-hakstol-of-head-coaching-duties--philadelphia-flyers/c-303020846 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181218010618/https://www.nhl.com/flyers/news/flyers-relieve-dave-hakstol-of-head-coaching-duties--philadelphia-flyers/c-303020846 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 18, 2018 |website=NHL.com |access-date=December 17, 2018 |date=December 17, 2018}}</ref> Hakstol served as head coach since the 2015–16 season, leading the team to a 134–101–42 record and two playoff appearances. |[[Gabe Kapler]]

Mackanin had a record of {{Winpct|174|238|record=y}} in his two and a half seasons as manager with no playoff appearances. It also was announced that he would remain with the organization as a special assistant to the general manager.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/phillies/pete-mackanin-philadelphia-phillies-manager-special-assistant-20170929.html|title=Phillies fire Pete Mackanin as manager|first=Matt|last=Gelb|newspaper=Philadelphia Inquirer|access-date=September 30, 2017|archive-date=October 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171003064059/http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/phillies/pete-mackanin-philadelphia-phillies-manager-special-assistant-20170929.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On October 29, 2017, the Phillies announced the hire of former Dodgers' Director of Development Gabe Kapler. He had no previous major league managerial or coaching experience.<ref>{{cite web|title=Phillies tap Dodgers exec Gabe Kapler as next manager|url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/21222460|website=[[ESPN]]|date=October 30, 2017|access-date=October 30, 2017|archive-date=November 6, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171106010638/http://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/21222460|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
!scope="row" style="text-align:center;" |[[New York Mets]]
|[[Terry Collins]]
|Retired
|[[Mickey Callaway]]
|style="text-align:left;" |Collins announced on October 1, 2017, that he would retire after the last game of the season and move to the Mets' front office. Collins finished with a {{Winpct|551|583|record=y}} record in seven years with club, with two playoff appearances in 2015 and 2016, in which they lost to the [[Kansas City Royals]] in the [[2015 World Series|World Series]] and lost the [[2016 National League Wild Card Game|Wild Card]] to the [[San Francisco Giants]] in the following season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/mets/news/mets-terry-collins-resigns-after-game-c257021012|title=Collins resigns, set to move to front-office role|date=October 1, 2017|first=Anthony|last=DiComo|website=MLB.com|access-date=January 25, 2020|archive-date=January 25, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200125122055/https://www.mlb.com/mets/news/mets-terry-collins-resigns-after-game-c257021012|url-status=live}}</ref> The Mets named [[Cleveland Indians]] pitching coach Mickey Callaway as their new manager on October 22, 2017. Callaway had no previous managerial experience.<ref>{{cite web|title=Indians pitching coach Mick Callaway to be Mets' new manager|url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/21114731|website=[[ESPN]]|date=October 22, 2017|access-date=October 22, 2017|archive-date=October 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171026194458/http://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/21114731|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
!scope="row" style="text-align:center;" |[[Boston Red Sox]]
|[[John Farrell (manager)|John Farrell]]
|Fired
|[[Alex Cora]]
|style="text-align:left;" |Farrell was fired on October 11, 2017. Farrell during his five years as manager compiled a {{Winpct|432|378|record=y}} record and earned three division titles in 2013, 2016 and 2017. He led the Red Sox to the [[2013 World Series]] title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/red-sox-dismiss-john-farrell-c258211184|title=Red Sox dismiss Farrell after five seasons|first=Ian|last=Browne|work=MLB.com|date=October 11, 2017|access-date=January 25, 2020|archive-date=October 29, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171029013559/http://m.mlb.com/news/article/258211184/red-sox-dismiss-john-farrell/|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Houston Astros]] bench coach [[Alex Cora]] was named manager on October 22, 2017, and formally assumed the role after the Astros' win in the [[2017 World Series]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://mlb.com/news/article/259274274/red-sox-name-alex-cora-manager/|title=Sox finalize 3-year deal with Cora to manage|last=Browne|first=Ian|date=October 22, 2017|work=MLB.com|access-date=October 23, 2017}}{{Dead link|date=June 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He had no previous managerial experience.
|-
!scope="row" style="text-align:center;" |[[Washington Nationals]]
|[[Dusty Baker]]
|rowspan=2 style="text-align:center;" |Contract not renewed
|[[Dave Martinez]]
|style="text-align:left;" |The Nationals announced on October 20, 2017, that Baker would not be returning for the 2018 season. Baker led the Nationals to the postseason in each of his two seasons with the club but couldn't get past the NLDS. The Nationals were {{Winning percentage|192|132|record=y}} under Baker.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dusty Baker won't return as Nationals manager|url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/21090820|website=[[ESPN]]|date=October 20, 2017|access-date=October 20, 2017|archive-date=October 23, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023174057/http://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/21090820|url-status=live}}</ref> The Nationals hired [[Dave Martinez]] to be their new manager on October 29, 2017. Martinez was previously the bench coach for the [[Chicago Cubs]] and had no managerial experience.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sources: Davey Martinez is Nationals' next pick for manager|url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/21210652|date=October 29, 2017|work=ESPN.com|access-date=October 29, 2017|first=Eddie|last=Matz|archive-date=November 4, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171104054459/http://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/21210652|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
!scope="row" style="text-align:center;" |[[New York Yankees]]
|[[Joe Girardi]]
|[[Aaron Boone]]
|style="text-align:left;" |The Yankees announced on October 26, 2017, that Girardi would not return for the 2018 season. Girardi led the Yankees to three division titles and one World Series championship during his ten years of managing the club. The Yankees were {{Winpct|910|710|record=y}} under Girardi.<ref>{{cite web|first=Bryan|last=Hoch|title=Girardi out as Yankees manager after 10 years|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/girardi-out-as-yankees-manager-c259741066|work=MLB.com|publisher=[[MLB]]|access-date=October 26, 2017|date=October 26, 2017|archive-date=October 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171026182930/http://m.mlb.com/news/article/259741066/girardi-out-as-yankees-manager/|url-status=live}}</ref> On December 1, 2017, former professional baseball player Aaron Boone was hired as the team's new manager.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/21634728|title=Aaron Boone become next manager of the New York Yankees/|work=ESPN.com|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=December 1, 2017|date=December 1, 2017}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> He had no previous coaching or managerial experience.
|}

| Price was fired on April 19 after starting the season with a {{Winning percentage|3|15|record=y}} record. In four seasons, Price finished with a {{Winning percentage|279|387|record=y}} record with no playoff appearances. [[Coach (baseball)#Bench coach|Bench coach]] Jim Riggleman was selected as the interim manager. His previous managerial experience included stints with the Padres, Cubs, Mariners, and Nationals. He had been a manager in the Reds' minor league system since 2012.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Sheldon|first1=Mark|title=Reds dismiss Price; Riggleman named interim|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/bryan-price-dismissed-as-reds-manager/c-272898702|website=mlb.com|publisher=[[MLB]]|access-date=April 19, 2018|archive-date=April 20, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180420010426/https://www.mlb.com/news/bryan-price-dismissed-as-reds-manager/c-272898702|url-status=live}}</ref> On October 21, 2018, the Reds named David Bell as their new manager, signing him to a three-year contract with a club option for 2022.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Sheldon|first1=Mark|title=Reds name David Bell new manager|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/reds-select-david-bell-as-teams-new-manager/c-299427658|website=MLB.com|publisher=[[MLB]]|date=October 21, 2018|access-date=October 21, 2018}}</ref>
|-
| style="text-align:center;"|[[St. Louis Cardinals]]
| style="text-align:center;"|[[Mike Matheny]]
| style="text-align:center;"|[[Mike Shildt]]
| style="text-align:center;"|Mike Shildt
| Matheny was fired on July 14 after starting the season with a {{Winning percentage|47|46|record=y}} record. In seven seasons, Matheny finished with a {{Winning percentage|591|473|record=y}} record with four playoff appearances, winning the National League pennant in 2013. Hitting coach John Mabry and assistant hitting coach Bill Mueller were also dismissed, and bench coach Mike Shildt was named interim manager. Shildt had no major league managing experience but had managed in the Cardinals minor league system.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Langosch|first1=Jenifer|title=Cardinals dismiss manager Matheny|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/cardinals-dismiss-manager-mike-matheny/c-285883856|website=mlb.com|publisher=[[MLB]]|access-date=July 14, 2018|archive-date=July 24, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180724071330/https://www.mlb.com/news/cardinals-dismiss-manager-mike-matheny/c-285883856|url-status=live}}</ref> On August 28, Shildt's "interim" title was dropped as he was named the new Cardinals manager.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Langosch|first1=Jenifer|title=Cards remove interim tag, name Shildt manager|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/cardinals-name-mike-shildt-manager/c-292290832|website=MLB.com|publisher=[[MLB]]|date=August 28, 2018|access-date=August 28, 2018|archive-date=October 20, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181020091130/https://www.mlb.com/news/cardinals-name-mike-shildt-manager/c-292290832|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
| style="text-align:center;"|[[Texas Rangers (baseball)|Texas Rangers]]
| style="text-align:center;"|[[Jeff Banister]]
| style="text-align:center;"|[[Don Wakamatsu]]
| style="text-align:center;"|[[Chris Woodward]]
| Banister was fired on September 21 after four seasons with a record of {{Winning percentage|325|313|record=y}} record. Banister finished in first place in his first two seasons as manager and amassed a {{Winning percentage|2|6|record=y}} in the playoffs. [[Coach (baseball)#Bench coach|Bench coach]] Don Wakamatsu was selected as the interim manager.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/jeff-banister-out-as-rangers-manager/c-295484568|title=Jeff Banister out as Rangers manager|website=MLB.com|access-date=September 21, 2018|archive-date=September 22, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180922024404/https://www.mlb.com/news/jeff-banister-out-as-rangers-manager/c-295484568|url-status=live}}</ref> On November 2, it was announced that Los Angeles Dodgers third-base coach Chris Woodward would be named the Rangers manager.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Sullivan|first1=TR|title=Woodward named Rangers' new manager|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/chris-woodward-to-be-named-rangers-manager/c-300171108|website=MLB.com|publisher=[[MLB]]|date=November 2, 2018|access-date=November 3, 2018|archive-date=November 3, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181103063120/https://www.mlb.com/news/chris-woodward-to-be-named-rangers-manager/c-300171108|url-status=live}}</ref>
|}

| Rivera was fired on December 3, after going {{winpct|record=y|5|7|0}} in the first 13 weeks of the season. ===General Manager of the Year Award=== On November 19, 2019, the NHL announced it would rename the General Manager of the Year Award in honour of [[Jim Gregory (ice hockey)|Jim Gregory]], the recently deceased former general manager of the [[Toronto Maple Leafs]] and former NHL executive. The official name is changed to the "[[Jim Gregory General Manager of the Year Award]]."{{cite press release |author=NHL Public Relations |publisher=NHL |website=nhl.com |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/nhl-renames-general-manager-award-for-jim-gregory-311501514 |title=NHL renames general manager award for Gregory |date=November 19, 2019 |access-date=November 19, 2019 |archive-date=December 11, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191211104112/https://www.nhl.com/news/nhl-renames-general-manager-award-for-jim-gregory/c-311501514 |url-status=live }} ==Coaching changes== {| class="wikitable" |+ Coaching changes ! colspan="4"|Off–season |- ! style="width:13%;"|Team ! style="width:11%;"|2018–19 coach ! style="width:10%;"|2019–20 coach ! | Rivera was fired on December 3, 2019, after going {{winpct|record=y|5|7}} in the first 12 games of the season. In 8+ seasons as the Panthers head coach, he went {{winpct|record=y|79|67|1}}, with four playoff appearances including three [[NFC South]] division titles and one Super Bowl appearance.
Fewell, the defensive backs coach, took over on an interim basis and went 0–4 the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Newton|first1=Daniel|title=Panthers owner David Tepper on Ron Rivera firing: 'I thought it was time'|date=December 3, 2019|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/28219337/ron-rivera-carolina-coach-nine-seasons|publisher=ESPN|access-date=December 3, 2019 |archive-date=December 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191203204118/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/28219337/ron-rivera-carolina-coach-nine-seasons |url-status=live}}</ref>

Rhule, who spent the previous seven seasons as college football head coach of [[Temple Owls football|Temple]] and [[Baylor Bears football|Baylor]] with a {{winpct|record=y|47|43}} record, was hired on January 7.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sources: Baylor's Matt Rhule to be Panthers' next coach, gets 7-year, $60 million deal|date=January 7, 2020|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/28439690/sources-panthers-agree-baylor-coach-matt-rhule|publisher=ESPN|access-date=January 7, 2020 |archive-date=January 8, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200108184242/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/28439690/sources-panthers-agree-baylor-coach-matt-rhule |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers reach agreement with Matt Rhule to become head coach|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/carolina-panthers-matt-rhule-agreement-head-coach|website=panthers.com|access-date=January 7, 2020 |archive-date=January 8, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200108071147/https://www.panthers.com/news/carolina-panthers-matt-rhule-agreement-head-coach |url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
! scope="row" style="text-align:center;" |[[Cleveland Browns]]
| style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"|{{sortname|Freddie|Kitchens}}
| style="text-align:center;" |{{sortname|Kevin|Stefanski}}
| Kitchens was fired on December 29, 2019, after going {{winpct|record=y|6|10}} in one season as head coach.<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns relieve Freddie Kitchens of duties as head coach|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-relieve-freddie-kitchens-of-duties-as-head-coach|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|access-date=December 30, 2019 |archive-date=December 30, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191230010620/https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-relieve-freddie-kitchens-of-duties-as-head-coach |url-status=live}}</ref>
Stefanski, who previously served as the offensive coordinator for the [[Minnesota Vikings]], was hired on January 13. He was on the Vikings staff for 14 years.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/kevin-stefanski-named-browns-head-coach|title=Kevin Stefanski named Browns head coach|date=January 13, 2020|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|access-date=January 13, 2020|archive-date=January 13, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200113233119/https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/kevin-stefanski-named-browns-head-coach|url-status=live}}</ref> This was his first head coaching position at any level. 
|-
! scope="row" style="text-align:center;" |[[Dallas Cowboys]]
| style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"|{{sortname|Jason|Garrett}}
| style="text-align:center;" |{{sortname|Mike|McCarthy}}
| style="text-align:center;" |Contract expired
| On January 5, the Cowboys announced they would not renew Garrett's contract, which expired January 14. The Cowboys were {{winpct|record=y|85|67}} in 9{{frac|1|2}} seasons under Garrett, making the playoffs 3 times but never advancing past the divisional round.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Archer|first1=Todd|title=Cowboys announce they won't renew Jason Garrett's contract|date=January 5, 2020|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/28429547/cowboys-announce-renew-jason-garrett-contract|publisher=ESPN|access-date=January 6, 2020 |archive-date=January 6, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200106010138/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/28429547/cowboys-announce-renew-jason-garrett-contract |url-status=live}}</ref>
McCarthy was hired as the Cowboys' new coach on January 6. In 12+ seasons as the [[Green Bay Packers]] head coach, he had a record of {{winpct|135|85|2|record=y}} with nine playoff appearances and one Super Bowl title.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Shook|first1=NIck|title=Cowboys expected to hire Mike McCarthy as new coach|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/mike-mccarthy-signs-five-year-deal-to-be-cowboys-hc-0ap3000001094867|publisher=National Football League|access-date=January 6, 2020 |archive-date=January 7, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200107031353/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001094867/article/cowboys-expected-to-hire-mike-mccarthy-as-new-coach |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Phillips|first1=Rob|title=Mike McCarthy Officially Hired As Head Coach|url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/mike-mccarthy-officially-hired-as-head-coach|website=dallascowboys.com|publisher=[[Dallas Cowboys]]|access-date=January 7, 2020 |archive-date=January 7, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200107231103/https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/mike-mccarthy-officially-hired-as-head-coach |url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
! scope="row" style="text-align:center;" |[[New York Giants]]
| colspan="2" style="text-align:center;" |{{sortname|Pat|Shurmur}}
| style="text-align:center;" |{{sortname|Joe|Judge|dab=American football}}
| rowspan="2" style="text-align:center;" |Fired
| Shurmur was fired on December 30, 2019, after going {{winpct|record=y|9|23}} in two seasons as the Giants' head coach, with no playoff appearances.<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants part ways with Head Coach Pat Shurmur|url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-part-ways-with-head-coach-pat-shurmur|website=Giants.com|access-date=December 30, 2019 |archive-date=December 30, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191230182934/https://www.giants.com/news/giants-part-ways-with-head-coach-pat-shurmur |url-status=live}}</ref>
Judge was hired on January 8, after serving as the special teams coordinator for the [[New England Patriots]] from 2015 to 2019, as well as the wide receivers coach in 2019. This is his first head coaching position at any level.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sources: Giants to hire Patriots' Joe Judge as head coach|date=January 7, 2020|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/28440034/sources-giants-deal-hire-patriots-joe-judge-head-coach|publisher=ESPN|access-date=January 7, 2020 |archive-date=January 12, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200112141144/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/28440034/sources-giants-deal-hire-patriots-joe-judge-head-coach |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.giants.com/news/joe-judge-hired-new-head-coach-new-england-patriots-special-teams-coordinator?campaign=sf:fanshare:facebook|title=Giants hire Joe Judge as head coach|website=giants.com|access-date=July 15, 2020|archive-date=January 12, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200112142702/https://www.giants.com/news/joe-judge-hired-new-head-coach-new-england-patriots-special-teams-coordinator?campaign=sf:fanshare:facebook|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
! scope="row" style="text-align:center;" |[[Washington Football Team]]
| style="text-align:center;" |{{sortname|Jay|Gruden}}
| style="text-align:center;" |{{sortname|Bill|Callahan|dab=American football coach}}
| style="text-align:center;" |{{sortname|Ron|Rivera}}
| After an 0–5 start, Gruden was fired on October 7, 2019. He had a {{winpct|35|49|1|record=y}} record for his 5+ season tenure with the organization, with one playoff appearance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.redskins.com/news/redskins-relieve-head-coach-jay-gruden-of-his-duties|title=Redskins Relieve Head Coach Jay Gruden Of His Duties|work=Redskins.com|date=October 7, 2019|access-date=October 7, 2019|archive-date=October 7, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191007120919/https://www.redskins.com/news/redskins-relieve-head-coach-jay-gruden-of-his-duties|url-status=live}}</ref> 
Callahan, the team's assistant head coach/offensive line coach, was previously the head coach of the [[Oakland Raiders]] in 2002 and 2003, with a record of {{winpct|15|17|record=y}} and one Super Bowl appearance; he finished out the 2019 season with a {{winpct|record=y|3|8}} record.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/redskins-fire-head-coach-jay-gruden-after-0-5-start-0ap3000001063290|title=Redskins fire head coach Jay Gruden after 0–5 starts|first=Grant|last=Gordon|publisher=National Football League|date=October 7, 2019|access-date=October 7, 2019|archive-date=October 14, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191014084224/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001063290/article/redskins-fire-head-coach-jay-gruden-after-05-start|url-status=live}}</ref>

Rivera, who had spent most of the previous nine seasons as head coach of the [[Carolina Panthers]], was hired on January 1, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Shook|first1=Nick|title=Ron Rivera hired as new Washington Redskins coach|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/ron-rivera-hired-as-new-washington-redskins-coach-0ap3000001093440|publisher=National Football League|access-date=December 31, 2019 |archive-date=December 31, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191231142839/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001093440/article/ron-rivera-hired-as-new-washington-redskins-coach |url-status=live}}</ref>
|}

On October 25, 2019, the Red Sox hired the 36-year-old [[Chaim Bloom]] as Chief Baseball Officer, succeeding Dombrowski as head of their baseball operations, with Brian O'Halloran named general manager and reporting to Bloom.{{cite news |url=https://www.masslive.com/redsox/2019/10/chaim-bloom-will-be-boston-red-soxs-chief-baseball-officer-brian-ohalloran-will-reportedly-become-gm.html |title=Chaim Bloom will be Boston Red Sox's chief baseball officer; Brian O'Halloran will reportedly become GM |website=masslive.com |first=Chris |last=Cotillo |date=October 25, 2019 |access-date=October 25, 2019 |archive-date=October 25, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191025235408/https://www.masslive.com/redsox/2019/10/chaim-bloom-will-be-boston-red-soxs-chief-baseball-officer-brian-ohalloran-will-reportedly-become-gm.html |url-status=live }} |- !scope="row" style="text-align:center;"|[[Pittsburgh Pirates]] |[[Neal Huntington]] | [[Ben Cherington]] | style="text-align:left;" | Huntington was fired on October 28, 2019. Huntington had been the longest-tenured general manager in the National League, as he was hired in September 2007. The Pirates made the playoffs three times during Huntington's tenure after the 2013, 2014 and 2015 seasons.{{cite web|last=Berry |first=Adam |url=https://www.mlb.com/pirates/news/neal-huntington-out-as-pirates-gm |title=Neal Huntington out as Pirates GM | Pittsburgh Pirates |work=Mlb.com |date=October 28, 2019 |access-date=January 1, 2020}} Ben Cherington was hired as the new general manager of the Pirates on November 18, 2019.{{cite web |last=Berry |first=Adam |url=https://www.mlb.com/pirates/news/ben-cherington-offered-pirates-gm-job |title=Ben Cherington named Pirates GM | Pittsburgh Pirates |work=Mlb.com |date=November 18, 2019 |access-date=January 1, 2020 |archive-date=December 16, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191216163216/https://www.mlb.com/pirates/news/ben-cherington-offered-pirates-gm-job |url-status=live }} |- !scope="row" style="text-align:center;"|[[Houston Astros]] | [[Jeff Luhnow]] | [[James Click]] | style="text-align:left;" | On January 13, Luhnow was suspended for the 2020 season after the Houston Astros were involved an investigation over the [[Houston Astros sign stealing scandal|use of technology to steal signs]] during their 2017 championship season. He was then fired by the Astros organization. James Click was named the new GM on February 3. He has spent the past 14 years in the Tampa Bay Rays front office.{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/james-click-named-astros-general-manager|title=Astros name James Click general manager|website=MLB.com}} |} ===Field managers=== ====Offseason==== {|class="wikitable plainrowheaders" style="text-align:center;" |- ! scope="col" | Team ! scope="col" | Former manager ! scope="col" | Interim manager ! scope="col" | Reason for leaving ! scope="col" | New manager ! scope="col" | Notes |- ! scope="row" | [[San Diego Padres]] | [[Andy Green (baseball)|Andy Green]] | [[Rod Barajas]] | style="text-align:center;"| Fired | [[Jayce Tingler]] | style="text-align:left;" | On September 21, 2019, Green was fired after four seasons with a record of {{Winning percentage|274|366|record=y}} with no playoff appearances. Bench coach [[Rod Barajas]] was named the interim manager of the Padres for the rest of the season.{{cite web|url=http://espn.com/mlb/story/padres-fire-green-after-four-sub-500-seasons|title=Padres Fire Green After Four Sub 500 Seasons|website=ESPN.com|date=September 21, 2019|access-date=September 21, 2019}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Tingler was named the new manager on October 28, 2019. Tingler had spent the previous five years in the [[Texas Rangers (baseball)|Texas Rangers]] organization as a coach and a front office executive.{{cite web |author=AJ Cassavell |url=https://www.mlb.com/padres/news/jayce-tingler-named-padres-manager |title=Jayce Tingler named Padres manager | San Diego Padres |work=Mlb.com |date=October 31, 2019 |access-date=January 1, 2020 |archive-date=December 13, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191213093217/https://www.mlb.com/padres/news/jayce-tingler-named-padres-manager |url-status=live }} |- ! scope="row" | [[San Francisco Giants]] | [[Bruce Bochy]] | rowspan="9" style="text-align:center;"| N/A | rowspan="2" style="text-align:center;"| Retired | [[Gabe Kapler]] | style="text-align:left;" | On February 18, 2019, Bochy announced he would retire following the conclusion of the 2019 season after 13 seasons. He led the Giants to three World Series championships in four playoff appearances. Bochy finished his Giants career with a {{Winning percentage|1052|1054|record=y}} record.{{cite web |last=Guardado |first=Maria |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/bruce-bochy-will-retire-after-2019-season-c304113650 |title=Bruce Bochy will retire after 2019 season |work=MLB.com |date=February 18, 2019 |access-date=January 1, 2020 |archive-date=March 28, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328193754/https://www.mlb.com/news/bruce-bochy-will-retire-after-2019-season-c304113650 |url-status=live }} On November 12, 2019, Gabe Kapler, who managed the Philadelphia Phillies for the past two seasons, was announced as the new manager.{{cite web |last=Guardado |first=Maria |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/gabe-kapler-giants-manager |title=Gabe Kapler hired as Giants manager |work=MLB.com |date=November 13, 2019 |access-date=January 1, 2020 |archive-date=December 16, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191216161818/https://www.mlb.com/news/gabe-kapler-giants-manager |url-status=live }} |- ! scope="row" | [[Kansas City Royals]] | [[Ned Yost]] | [[Mike Matheny]] | style="text-align:left;" | On September 23, 2019, Yost announced that he would retire at the end of the 2019 season. He led the Royals to consecutive World Series appearances in 2014 and 2015, winning the championship in 2015. He had been the manager since May 2010. Yost finished his career in Kansas City with a {{Winning percentage|746|839|record=y}} record.{{cite web |last=Flanagan |first=Jeffrey |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/ned-yost-retires-as-royals-manager |title=Ned Yost retires as Royals manager |work=MLB.com |date=September 23, 2019 |access-date=January 1, 2020 |archive-date=July 24, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200724175342/https://www.mlb.com/news/ned-yost-retires-as-royals-manager |url-status=live }} On October 31, 2019, Mike Matheny, who spent last season as the special advisor to Royals general manager [[Dayton Moore]], was named the new manager of the Kansas City Royals. Matheny managed the [[St. Louis Cardinals]] from 2012 through mid-July 2018. He had a career record of {{Winning percentage|591|474|record=y}}. He led the Cardinals to the postseason in his first four seasons as manager and won the National League pennant in 2013.{{Cite press release |title=Royals Name Mike Matheny 17th Manager in Franchise History |date=2019-10-31 |publisher=Kansas City Royals |url=https://www.mlb.com/press-release/royals-name-mike-matheny-17th-manager-in-franchise-history |via=MLB.com |access-date=2025-03-09 |archive-date=April 14, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250414015642/https://www.mlb.com/press-release/royals-name-mike-matheny-17th-manager-in-franchise-history |url-status=live }}{{cite web|last=Flanagan |first=Jeffrey |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/mike-matheny-to-be-royals-new-manager |title=Mike Matheny to be Royals new manager |work=MLB.com |date=October 31, 2019 |access-date=January 1, 2020}} |- ! scope="row" | [[Chicago Cubs]] | [[Joe Maddon]] | Contract not renewed | [[David Ross (baseball)|David Ross]] | style="text-align:left;" | On September 29, 2019, the Cubs announced that they would not offer Maddon a contract extension following this season. He led the Cubs to four playoff appearances in five years, including the 2016 World Series championship, the Cubs' first since 1908. Maddon finished his tenure with the Cubs with a record of {{Winning percentage|471|339|record=y}}.{{cite web |last=Bastian |first=Jordan |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/joe-maddon-not-returning-as-cubs-manager |title=Joe Maddon not returning as Cubs manager |work=MLB.com |date=September 29, 2019 |access-date=January 1, 2020 |archive-date=December 26, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191226023349/https://www.mlb.com/news/joe-maddon-not-returning-as-cubs-manager |url-status=live }} Ross, who was a member of the 2016 World Series winning team under Maddon, was named as his replacement on October 24, 2019. Ross spent the last three seasons as the special assistant to baseball operations for the team as well as a baseball analyst for ESPN.{{cite web |last=Bastian |first=Jordan |url=https://www.mlb.com/cubs/news/david-ross-next-cubs-manager |title=David Ross next Cubs manager | Chicago Cubs |work=Mlb.com |date=October 24, 2019 |access-date=January 1, 2020 |archive-date=November 5, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191105081017/https://www.mlb.com/cubs/news/david-ross-next-cubs-manager |url-status=live }} |- ! scope="row" | [[Pittsburgh Pirates]] | [[Clint Hurdle]] | rowspan="3" | Fired | [[Derek Shelton]] | style="text-align:left;" | On September 29, 2019, the Pirates announced that they dismissed Hurdle after nine seasons with a record of {{Winning percentage|735|720|record=y}} with three playoff appearances.{{cite web |last=Berry |first=Adam |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/clint-hurdle-dismissed-by-pirates |title=Clint Hurdle dismissed by Pirates |work=MLB.com |date=September 29, 2019 |access-date=January 1, 2020 |archive-date=January 21, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200121145034/https://www.mlb.com/news/clint-hurdle-dismissed-by-pirates |url-status=live }} On November 27, 2019, Shelton, who spent the previous two seasons as the bench coach for the [[Minnesota Twins]], was named the manager of the Pittsburgh Pirates.{{cite web |last=Berry |first=Adam |url=https://www.mlb.com/pirates/news/derek-shelton-named-pirates-manager |title=Derek Shelton named Pirates manager | Pittsburgh Pirates |work=Mlb.com |date=December 4, 2019 |access-date=January 1, 2020 |archive-date=December 25, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191225200723/https://www.mlb.com/pirates/news/derek-shelton-named-pirates-manager |url-status=live }} He also spent time as a hitting coach for the [[Cleveland Indians]] from 2005 to 2009 and a hitting coach for the [[Tampa Bay Rays]] from 2010 to 2016 while also serving as a quality control coach for the [[Toronto Blue Jays]] in 2017.{{cite web |date=November 27, 2019 |title=Pittsburgh Pirates Hire Derek Shelton As Manager |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/redsox/2019/11/27/log/AzNnddup7Aka6t95AlphOJ/story.html |access-date=2025-03-09 |website=Boston Globe |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=April 12, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250412150943/https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/redsox/2019/11/27/log/AzNnddup7Aka6t95AlphOJ/story.html |url-status=live }} |- ! scope="row" | [[Los Angeles Angels]] | [[Brad Ausmus]] | Joe Maddon | style="text-align:left;" | On September 30, 2019, Ausmus was fired after one season with a record of {{Winning percentage|72|90|record=y}}. Ausmus served as a special assistant to the Angels general manager [[Billy Eppler]] in the 2018 season.{{cite web|title=Ausmus out in LA; Maddon up next?|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/brad-ausmus-dismissed-as-angels-manager|website=MLB.com|date=September 30, 2019|access-date=September 30, 2019|archive-date=September 30, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190930214354/https://www.mlb.com/news/brad-ausmus-dismissed-as-angels-manager|url-status=live}} Maddon was hired by the Angels on October 16, 2019.{{cite web |last=Bollinger |first=Rhett |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/joe-maddon-angels-manager |title=Joe Maddon named Angels manager |work=MLB.com |date=October 21, 2019 |access-date=January 1, 2020 |archive-date=October 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191021164132/https://www.mlb.com/news/joe-maddon-angels-manager |url-status=live }} Maddon had spent 31 years in the Angels organization (12 years as a coach) before managing the [[Tampa Bay Rays]] for nine years and the [[Chicago Cubs]] for five years. |- ! scope="row" rowspan="2"|[[New York Mets]] | [[Mickey Callaway]] | [[Carlos Beltrán]] | style="text-align:left;" | On October 3, 2019, Callaway was fired after two seasons with a record of {{Winning percentage|163|161|record=y}} with no playoff appearances.{{cite web|last=DiComo|first=Anthony|title=Mets part ways with manager Mickey Callaway|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/mets-dismiss-manager-mickey-callaway|website=MLB.com|date=October 3, 2019|access-date=October 3, 2019|archive-date=October 11, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191011225120/https://www.mlb.com/news/mets-dismiss-manager-mickey-callaway|url-status=live}} On November 1, 2019, Carlos Beltrán, who played for the team from 2005 to the middle of the 2011 season, was named the new manager of the team. Beltrán was a special adviser to the [[New York Yankees]] general manager [[Brian Cashman]] last season.{{cite web |author=Anthony DiComo |url=https://www.mlb.com/mets/news/carlos-beltran-to-be-new-mets-manager |title=Carlos Beltran is new Mets manager | New York Mets |work=Mlb.com |date=November 1, 2019 |access-date=January 1, 2020 |archive-date=November 5, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191105071920/https://www.mlb.com/mets/news/carlos-beltran-to-be-new-mets-manager |url-status=live }} |- | Carlos Beltrán | Mutual Decision | [[Luis Rojas (baseball)|Luis Rojas]] | style="text-align:left;" | On January 16, Beltran and the Mets agreed to part ways before managing a game for the Mets, in light of his reported involvement in the [[Houston Astros sign stealing scandal|Astros using cameras to steal signs]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/28496773/mets-agree-part-ways-manager-carlos-beltran|title=Mets agree to part ways with manager Beltran|date=January 16, 2020|website=ESPN.com|access-date=March 13, 2020|archive-date=January 17, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200117001224/https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/28496773/mets-agree-part-ways-manager-carlos-beltran|url-status=live}} The Mets hired Rojas on January 22. He had spent the last 13 years in the Mets organization.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/28549037/mets-make-official-announce-luis-rojas-new-manager|title=New Mets manager Rojas ready to 'work tirelessly'|date=January 24, 2020|website=ESPN.com|access-date=January 24, 2020|archive-date=January 24, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200124052244/https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/28549037/mets-make-official-announce-luis-rojas-new-manager|url-status=live}} |- ! scope="row" | [[Philadelphia Phillies]] | Gabe Kapler | rowspan="2" |Fired | [[Joe Girardi]] | style="text-align:left;" | On October 10, 2019, Kapler was fired after two seasons with a record of {{Winning percentage|161|163|record=y}} with no playoff appearances.{{cite web|title=Philadelphia Phillies fire manager Gabe Kapler|url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/27813181/philadelphia-phillies-fire-manager-gabe-kapler|website=ESPN.com|date=October 10, 2019|access-date=October 10, 2019|archive-date=October 10, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191010145014/https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/27813181/philadelphia-phillies-fire-manager-gabe-kapler|url-status=live}} Girardi, who served as a baseball analyst for the MLB Network the last two seasons, was hired as new manager on October 24, 2019. Girardi previously managed the [[Florida Marlins]] for the 2006 season and the [[New York Yankees]] from 2008 to 2017.{{cite web |last=Zolecki |first=Todd |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/joe-girardi-hired-to-be-phillies-manager |title=Joe Girardi hired to be Phillies manager |work=MLB.com |date=October 24, 2019 |access-date=January 1, 2020 |archive-date=October 28, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191028175559/https://www.mlb.com/news/joe-girardi-hired-to-be-phillies-manager |url-status=live }} |- ! scope="row" | [[Houston Astros]] | [[A. J. Hinch]] | [[Dusty Baker]] | style="text-align:left;" | On January 13, Hinch was suspended by MLB for the 2020 season as part of an investigation against the [[Houston Astros sign stealing scandal|Astros using hidden cameras to steal signs]] during their [[2017 Houston Astros season|2017 championship season]]; he was fired by the Astros shortly after the suspension was announced. Hinch had a regular season record of {{winning percentage|481|329|record=y}} with a total of four postseason appearances compiling a record of {{Winning percentage|28|22|record=y}}, two World Series appearances, and a World Series championship in [[2017 World Series|2017]], throughout his tenure as Astros manager.{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/astros-sign-stealing-penalty|title=Astros' Luhnow, Hinch suspended for '20 season|work=MLB.com|date=January 13, 2020|access-date=January 13, 2020|archive-date=January 13, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200113192209/https://www.mlb.com/news/astros-sign-stealing-penalty|url-status=live}} On January 29, the Astros hired [[Dusty Baker]] to replace Hinch. He managed the [[San Francisco Giants]] from 1993 to 2002, the [[Chicago Cubs]] from 2003 to 2006, the [[Cincinnati Reds]] from 2008 to 2013, and the [[Washington Nationals]] during the 2016 and 2017 seasons. His overall managerial record is {{winpct|record=y|1863|1636}} in the regular season, and {{winpct|record=y|23|32}} in the playoffs, losing the [[2002 World Series]]. |- ! scope="row" | [[Boston Red Sox]] | [[Alex Cora]] | [[Ron Roenicke]] | Mutual Decision | Ron Roenicke | style="text-align:left;" |On January 14, the Red Sox and Cora officially agreed to part ways with each other after two seasons. Cora had been under investigation by MLB over the [[Houston Astros sign stealing scandal|Houston Astros' use of hidden cameras to steal signs]] during that team's 2017 championship season (while Cora was the bench coach) as well as under investigation of allegations that the Red Sox engaged in impermissible electronic sign stealing in 2018 (while Cora was the manager). In his two seasons as Red Sox manager, he compiled a record of {{winning percentage|192|132|record=y}}, winning the [[2018 World Series]].{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/alex-cora-dismissed-as-red-sox-manager|title=Red Sox part ways with manager Alex Cora|work=MLB.com|date=January 14, 2020|access-date=January 14, 2020|archive-date=January 15, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200115004501/https://www.mlb.com/news/alex-cora-dismissed-as-red-sox-manager|url-status=live}} Roenicke was promoted from bench coach to interim manager on February 11. A longtime coach, his only managerial experience was with the [[Milwaukee Brewers]] from 2011 to 2015, compiling a record of {{winpct|record=y|342|331}}, with one playoff appearance and a {{winpct|record=y|5|6}} record in the postseason.{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/ron-roenicke-red-sox-interim-manager|title=Roenicke named Boston's interim skipper|website=MLB.com|access-date=February 12, 2020|archive-date=February 13, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200213145812/https://www.mlb.com/news/ron-roenicke-red-sox-interim-manager|url-status=live}} On April 22, the "interim" tag was removed from Roenicke's title, following MLB's findings about the 2018 Red Sox, which focused on the team's video replay operator.{{cite news |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2020/04/22/sports/red-sox-remove-interim-tag-manager-ron-roenicke/ |title=Red Sox remove interim tag from manager Ron Roenicke |first=Julian |last=McWilliams |website=[[The Boston Globe]] |url-access=limited |date=April 22, 2020 |access-date=April 22, 2020 |archive-date=April 22, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200422232535/https://www.bostonglobe.com/2020/04/22/sports/red-sox-remove-interim-tag-manager-ron-roenicke/ |url-status=live }} |} ====In-season==== {|class="wikitable plainrowhedaers" style="text-align:center;" |- ! Team ! Former manager ! Interim manager ! Reason for leaving ! New manager ! Notes |- | [[Detroit Tigers]] | [[Ron Gardenhire]] | [[Lloyd McClendon]] | style="text-align:center;"| Retired | [[A. J. Hinch]] | style="text-align:left;" | On September 19, Gardenhire announced his immediate retirement due to health concerns. Lloyd McClendon was named interim manager for the rest of the season. Gardenhire finished his almost three-year tenure with a {{Winning percentage|132|241|record=y}} record and no playoff appearances.{{Cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/mlb/tigers/2020/09/19/detroit-tigers-ron-gardenhire-not-return-manager/5841294002/|title=Detroit Tigers' Ron Gardenhire retires as manager after nearly 3 seasons|first=Evan|last=Petzold|website=Detroit Free Press|access-date=September 19, 2020|archive-date=October 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201003104526/https://www.freep.com/story/sports/mlb/tigers/2020/09/19/detroit-tigers-ron-gardenhire-not-return-manager/5841294002/|url-status=live}} |}

===Major coach of the year awards=== *'''[[Associated Press College Basketball Coach of the Year|Associated Press Coach of the Year]]:''' [[Juwan Howard]], [[2020–21 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]]{{cite press release|url=https://apnews.com/article/nba-basketball-michigan-mick-cronin-coronavirus-pandemic-418d80c7fdd658fc43d4b2bbc7c07fd1|title=Michigan's Juwan Howard named AP college coach of the year|publisher=Associated Press |date=April 1, 2021 |access-date=April 1, 2021}} *'''[[Henry Iba Award]] ([[USBWA]]):''' Juwan Howard, Michigan{{cite press release|url=http://sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2021/iba210319.html |title=Michigan's Howard Wins Henry Iba Award |publisher=United States Basketball Writers Association |date=March 19, 2021 |access-date=March 19, 2021}} *'''[[NABC Coach of the Year]]:''' [[Mark Few]], [[2020–21 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]] *'''[[Naismith College Coach of the Year]]:''' Mark Few, Gonzaga{{cite press release|url=http://naismithtrophy.com/tara-vanderveer-and-mark-few-named-as-2021-werner-ladder-naismith-coach-of-the-year-honorees/ |title=Tara VanDerveer and Mark Few Named as 2021 Werner Ladder Naismith Coach of the Year Honorees |publisher=Atlanta Tipoff Club |date=April 2, 2021 |access-date=April 2, 2021}} * '''[[Sporting News Men's College Basketball Coach of the Year Award|''Sporting News'' Coach of the Year]]:''' Juwan Howard, Michigan{{cite news|last=DeCourcy|first=Mike|title=Michigan's Juwan Howard is Sporting News' 2020-21 Coach of the Year|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/juwan-howard-michigan-coach-of-the-year/1tb73ththc6h41piqjya53s4y5|access-date=March 9, 2021 |work=[[Sporting News]]|date=March 9, 2021}} ==Coaching changes== Fifty-six teams changed coaches during the season and after it ended. Two schools changed coaches between their first practice and first game of the season. One coach resigned and one died. {|class="wikitable" !Team !Former
coach !Interim

Two days later, assistant coach Robinson, who was hired by the team in September, was named interim head coach for the 2020–21 season.{{cite news |last=Bidwell |first=Jeff |date=November 17, 2020 |title=Robinson named UT Martin Interim Basketball coach |url=https://www.wpsdlocal6.com/sports/robinson-named-ut-martin-interim-basketball-coach/article_cb41f298-2929-11eb-8563-73134428eaef.html |access-date=November 17, 2020 |publisher=[[WPSD]] |location=[[Paducah, KY]]}} After Robinson was not retained at the end of the season, the school hired Bethune–Cookman head coach Ryan Ridder as its new coach on March 30. |- | [[UT Rio Grande Valley Vaqueros men's basketball|UTRGV]] | [[Lew Hill (basketball)|Lew Hill]] | [[Jai Steadman]] | [[Matt Figger]] | Hill died on February 7, 2021.{{cite news|url=https://www.midmajormadness.com/2021/2/7/22271659/utrgv-texas-rio-grande-valley-basketball-coach-lew-hill-passes-away|first=Russell|last=Steinberg|title=UTRGV head coach Lew Hill passes away|website=SB Nation|date=February 7, 2021|access-date=February 7, 2021}} The 55-year-old was in his fifth season as head coach at [[UT Rio Grande Valley Vaqueros men's basketball|Texas–Rio Grande Valley]], amassing a record of 67–75 during his tenure at the school and had been preparing to step down after the season due to ongoing medical issues, including a bout with COVID. Four days after Hill's death, assistant coach Steadman was named interim head coach of the Vaqueros for the rest of the season.{{cite news|url=https://www.valleycentral.com/sports/local-sports/utrgv-announces-jai-steadman-as-interim-mens-basketball-coach/|title=UTRGV announces Jai Steadman as interim men's basketball coach|publisher=KVEO-TV|first=Amanda|last=Atwell|date=February 11, 2021|access-date=February 15, 2021}} After the season ended, the school hired Austin Peay head coach Figger on March 29. |- | [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]] | [[Larry Krystkowiak]] | | [[Craig Smith (basketball, born 1972)|Craig Smith]] | Utah fired Krystowiak on March 16, 2021, after ten seasons with an overall record of 183–139.{{cite news|url=https://www.fox13now.com/sports/utes-fire-larry-krystkowiak-as-head-coach|first=Jeff|last=Tavss|title=Utes fire Larry Krystkowiak as head coach|publisher=[[KSTU]]|date=March 16, 2021|access-date=March 17, 2021}} The Utes hired Craig Smith from cross-state rival Utah State as their next head coach on March 27.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/utah-to-hire-utah-states-craig-smith-to-replace-larry-krystkowiak-as-utes-coach/|title=Utah to hire Utah State's Craig Smith to replace Larry Krystkowiak as Utes coach|website=cbssports.com|first=Matt|last=Norlander|date=March 27, 2021|access-date=March 28, 2021}} |- | [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]] | [[Craig Smith (basketball, born 1972)|Craig Smith]] | | [[Ryan Odom]] | Smith left Utah State after three seasons to take the head coaching position at cross-state rival Utah on March 27, 2021. ====Off-season====
* On June 2, 2021, the [[Boston Celtics]] head coach [[Brad Stevens]] was promoted to president of basketball operations following the retirement of [[Danny Ainge]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Danny Ainge Announces Retirement; Brad Stevens Promoted to President of Basketball Operations|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/danny-ainge-announces-retirement-brad-stevens-promoted-president-basketball|website=NBA.com|date=June 2, 2021|access-date=June 2, 2021}}</ref>
* On June 4, 2021, the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] and [[Terry Stotts]] had mutually agreed to part ways after nine seasons with the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers And Terry Stotts Mutually Agree To Part Ways|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-and-terry-stotts-mutually-agree-part-ways|website=NBA.com|date=June 4, 2021|accessdate=June 4, 2021}}</ref>
* On June 5, 2021, the [[Orlando Magic]] and [[Steve Clifford]] had mutually agreed to part ways after three seasons with the team.<ref>{{cite web |last=Brumbelow |first=Brooke |date=June 5, 2021 |title=Orlando Magic, Steve Clifford Mutually Agree to Part Ways |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-steve-clifford-mutually-agree-part-ways-20210605 |access-date=June 5, 2021 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>
* On June 9, 2021, the [[Indiana Pacers]] fired head coach [[Nate Bjorkgren]] after only one season with the team in which they missed the playoffs for the first time in six years.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pacers Announce Nate Bjorkgren Will Not Return as Coach|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/pacers-announce-nate-bjorkgren-will-not-return-coach|website=NBA.com|access-date=June 9, 2021|date=June 9, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Wojnarowski|first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski |title=Nate Bjorkgren fired as Indiana Pacers coach after playoff streak ends, sources say|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31597939|website=ESPN.com|access-date=June 9, 2021|date=June 9, 2021}}</ref>
* On June 16, 2021, the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] and head coach [[Stan Van Gundy]] had mutually agreed to part ways after only one season.<ref>{{cite web |date=June 16, 2021 |title=New Orleans Pelicans and Stan Van Gundy mutually agree to part ways |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/new-orleans-pelicans-and-stan-van-gundy-mutually-agree-part-ways |accessdate=June 16, 2021 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>
* On June 16, 2021, the [[Washington Wizards]] and head coach [[Scott Brooks]] part ways after five seasons with the team.<ref>{{cite web |last=Filyo |first=Jackson |date=June 16, 2021 |title=Wizards part ways with Brooks |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-part-ways-with-brooks |accessdate=June 16, 2021 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>
* On June 17, 2021, [[Rick Carlisle]] resigned from his position as head coach of the [[Dallas Mavericks]] after the 13 seasons with the team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rick Carlisle steps down as Mavericks coach |url=https://www.nba.com/news/rick-carlisle-wont-return-to-mavericks |website=NBA.com |access-date=June 18, 2021 |date=June 17, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Wojnarowski |first1=Adrian |last2=MacMahon |first2=Tim |name-list-style=and |date=June 17, 2021 |title=Rick Carlisle won't return as Dallas Mavericks coach after 13 seasons |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31654042 |access-date=January 24, 2022 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>
* On June 24, 2021, the Indiana Pacers rehired Rick Carlisle back as their new head coach for his second stint with the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pacers Reach Agreement with Rick Carlisle to Become Head Coach|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-reach-agreement-rick-carlisle-become-head-coach|website=NBA.com|date=June 24, 2021|access-date=June 24, 2021}}</ref>
* On June 27, 2021, the Portland Trail Blazers hired [[Chauncey Billups]] as their new head coach.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Name Chauncey Billups Head Coach|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2021/6/27/trail-blazers-name-chauncey-billups-head-coach|website=NBA.com|access-date=June 28, 2021|date=June 27, 2021}}</ref>
* On June 28, 2021, the Boston Celtics hired [[Ime Udoka]] as their new head coach.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Celtics Name Ime Udoka 18th Head Coach in Franchise History|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-name-ime-udoka-18th-head-coach-franchise-history|website=NBA.com|date=June 28, 2021|access-date=June 28, 2021}}</ref>
* On June 28, 2021, the Dallas Mavericks hired [[Jason Kidd]] as their new head coach.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sefko |first=Eddie |date=June 28, 2021 |title=Mavericks Sign Jason Kidd as New Head Coach |url=https://www.mavs.com/coach-kidd/ |access-date=June 28, 2021 |website=Mavs.com}}</ref>
* On July 7, 2021, the [[Atlanta Hawks]] hired [[Nate McMillan]] as full-time head coach.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Finberg |first=Annie |date=July 7, 2021 |title=Atlanta Hawks Name Nate McMillan Head Coach |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-name-nate-mcmillan-head-coach |access-date=July 8, 2021 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>
* On July 11, 2021, the Orlando Magic hired [[Jamahl Mosley]] as their new head coach.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brumbelow |first=Brooke |date=July 11, 2021 |title=Orlando Magic Name Jamahl Mosley Head Coach |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-name-jamahl-mosley-head-coach-20210711 |access-date=July 11, 2021 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

| style="text-align:left;" | On September 19, 2020, Gardenhire announced his retirement due to health concerns. Lloyd McClendon was named interim manager for the rest of the season that same day. Gardenhire finished with a {{winpct|132|241|record=y}} record in just under three seasons.  The Tigers did not make the playoffs during his tenure.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/29922184/detroit-tigers-manager-ron-gardenhire-retires-effective-immediately|title=Detroit Tigers manager Ron Gardenhire retires immediately to focus on health|website=ESPN.com|date=September 19, 2020|agency=[[Associated Press|AP]]|access-date=September 28, 2020|archive-date=October 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201003041244/https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/29922184/detroit-tigers-manager-ron-gardenhire-retires-effective-immediately|url-status=live}}</ref>  The Tigers hired A.J. Hinch on October 30 as their new manager.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/aj-hinch-hired-as-tigers-manager |title=Hinch: 'The good times are coming' to Detroit |first=Jason |last=Beck |website=[[MLB.com]] |date=October 30, 2020 |access-date=October 30, 2020 |archive-date=October 31, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201031094712/https://www.mlb.com/news/aj-hinch-hired-as-tigers-manager |url-status=live }}</ref> In seven seasons, Hinch has accumulated a {{winpct|570|472|record=y}} record while managing the Houston Astros and Arizona Diamondbacks.  He led the Astros to two World Series appearances, winning in [[2017 World Series|2017]] against the Los Angeles Dodgers and losing in [[2019 World Series|2019]] to the Washington Nationals, both in seven games.

| style="text-align:left;" | On September 27, 2020, the Red Sox announced that Roenicke would not be retained for the 2021 season after only one season following the team and [[Alex Cora]] parting ways.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://mlb.nbcsports.com/2020/09/27/ron-roenicke-fired-by-red-sox-after-one-season |title=Ron Roenicke Fired By Red Sox After One Season |website=[[NBCSports.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press|AP]] |date=September 27, 2020 |access-date=September 28, 2020 |archive-date=October 8, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201008101142/https://mlb.nbcsports.com/2020/09/27/ron-roenicke-fired-by-red-sox-after-one-season/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Roenicke finished his only season with a {{winpct|24|36|record=y}} record and did not make the postseason. Cora was re-hired on November 6 after serving a one-year suspension imposed by MLB for his role in the [[Houston Astros sign stealing scandal]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/alex-cora-red-sox-manager-returns |title=Cora back as Red Sox skipper on 2-year deal |first=Ian |last=Browne |website=[[MLB.com]] |date=November 6, 2020 |access-date=November 6, 2020 |archive-date=November 6, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201106145758/https://www.mlb.com/news/alex-cora-red-sox-manager-returns |url-status=live }}</ref>  Prior to his suspension, Cora was {{winpct|192|132|record=y}} in two seasons with the Red Sox, leading the team to a World Series win in his first season.
|-

| [[Rick Renteria]]
| style="text-align:center;"| Fired
| [[Tony La Russa]]
| style="text-align:left;" | On October 12, 2020, the White Sox announced that Renteria would not return, ending his tenure with the team after four years with one year remaining on his contract.  Renteria finished with a record of {{winpct|236|309|record=y}} and one playoff appearance.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Duber|first1=Vinnie|title=Sox part ways with Renteria, will have new manager in 2021|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/white-sox/white-sox-part-ways-rick-renteria-will-have-new-manager-2021|publisher=NBC Sports Chicago|access-date=October 15, 2020|archive-date=December 5, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201205083153/https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/white-sox/white-sox-part-ways-rick-renteria-will-have-new-manager-2021|url-status=live}}</ref> On October 29, it was announced that Tony La Russa would return to the White Sox as manager. La Russa managed the White Sox during 1979–1986, compiling a {{winpct|522|510|record=y}} record and one playoff appearance. At the age of 76, La Russa became the oldest manager in the majors. He had not managed any team since the [[2011 St. Louis Cardinals season|St. Louis Cardinals in 2011]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.mlb.com/news/tony-la-russa-named-white-sox-manager |title=Tony La Russa named White Sox manager |first=Scott |last=Merkin |website=[[MLB.com]] |date=October 29, 2020 |access-date=October 29, 2020 |archive-date=November 1, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201101031548/https://www.mlb.com/news/tony-la-russa-named-white-sox-manager |url-status=live }}</ref>

| Culley was fired on January 13 after one season with the Texans, finishing with a {{winpct|record=y|4|13}} record and missing the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=January 13, 2022 |title=Houston Texans fire head coach David Culley after one season |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/houston-texans-david-culley-fire-head-coach-after-one-season |access-date=January 13, 2022 |publisher=NFL Media |archive-date=January 13, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220113201823/https://www.nfl.com/news/houston-texans-david-culley-fire-head-coach-after-one-season |url-status=live }}</ref>

Smith, who spent the previous season as Houston's defensive coordinator and associate head coach, was hired on February 7. This was his third head coaching position in the NFL. As the head coach of the [[Chicago Bears]] from {{NFL year|2004|2012}}, the team's overall record was {{Winning percentage|81|63|record=y}}, with three playoff appearances, three [[NFC North]] division titles, an appearance in [[Super Bowl XLI]], and a {{Winpct|3|3|record=y}} playoff record. | Meyer was fired on December 16, 2021, due to a season full of on- and off-the-field issues. Bevell, the team's offensive coordinator since 2021, was promoted to interim head coach. This is his second head coaching position, after serving as interim head coach for the [[Detroit Lions]] in [[2020 Detroit Lions season|2020]], where he obtained a record of {{Winpct|1|4|record=y}}. He finished out the 2021 season with a {{winpct|1|3|record=y}} record.<ref name="MeyerBevell2" />

Pederson was hired on February 3. He was the head coach of the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] from 2016 to 2020 with a record of {{winpct|42|37|1|record=y}}, three playoff appearances with a record of {{winpct|4|2|record=y}}, two [[NFC East]] division titles, and the [[Super Bowl LII]] championship.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Oehser |first=John |date=February 3, 2022 |title=Official: Pederson hired as head coach |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/official-pederson-hired-as-head-coach |access-date=February 3, 2022 |publisher=NFL Media |location=[[Jacksonville]] |archive-date=February 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220204082414/https://www.jaguars.com/news/official-pederson-hired-as-head-coach |url-status=dead }}</ref>

| Gruden resigned on October 11, 2021, due to the publication of controversial emails prior to becoming the Raiders head coach. In Gruden's 3+ seasons during his second stint with Oakland/Las Vegas, the Raiders were {{winpct|record=y|22|31}} with no playoff appearances.<ref>{{Cite press release |date=October 11, 2021 |title=Jon Gruden Statement |publisher=NFL Media |location=[[Las Vegas]] |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/statement-from-jon-gruden |access-date=October 12, 2021 |archive-date=October 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211012021720/https://www.raiders.com/news/statement-from-jon-gruden |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=October 11, 2021 |title=Jon Gruden resigns as Las Vegas Raiders head coach |work=NFL.com |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/jon-gruden-resigns-as-las-vegas-raiders-head-coach |access-date=October 12, 2021 |archive-date=October 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211012011927/https://www.nfl.com/news/jon-gruden-resigns-as-las-vegas-raiders-head-coach |url-status=live }}</ref>
Bisaccia, the team's special teams coordinator and assistant head coach since 2018, was promoted to interim head coach. This was his first head coaching position after 20 years as an assistant coach in the NFL. He finished out the 2021 regular season with a {{winpct|7|5|record=y}} record, leading the Raiders to a [[2021–22 NFL playoffs#AFC: Cincinnati Bengals 26, Las Vegas Raiders 19|Wild Card playoff appearance]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 11, 2021 |title=Rich Bisaccia to serve as Interim Head Coach |work=Raiders.com |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/rich-bisaccia-to-serve-as-interim-head-coach |access-date=October 12, 2021 |archive-date=October 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211012025221/https://www.raiders.com/news/rich-bisaccia-to-serve-as-interim-head-coach |url-status=live }}</ref>

He was the head coach of the [[Denver Broncos]] from {{NFL year|2009|2010}} with a record of {{winpct|11|17|record=y}} and no playoff appearances.<ref>{{Cite news |date=January 31, 2022 |title=Raiders announce Josh McDaniels as next Head Coach |work=Raiders.com |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-hire-josh-mcdaniels-as-head-coach |access-date=January 31, 2022 |archive-date=January 31, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220131222839/https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-hire-josh-mcdaniels-as-head-coach |url-status=live }}</ref>

O'Connell, who spent the previous two seasons as the [[Los Angeles Rams]] offensive coordinator, was hired on February 16. He also won [[Associated Press NFL Coach of the Year Award|AP NFL Coach of the Year Award]] in {{NFL year|2006}}.<ref>{{Cite news |date=January 25, 2022 |title=New Orleans Saints head coach Sean Payton to step away |work=neworleanssaints.com |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/sean-payton-new-orleans-saints-head-coach-step-away-nfl-retirement-012522 |access-date=January 25, 2022 |archive-date=January 25, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220125212053/https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/sean-payton-new-orleans-saints-head-coach-step-away-nfl-retirement-012522 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=January 25, 2022 |title=Sean Payton stepping down as head coach of Saints after 15 seasons |work=NFL.com |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/sean-payton-stepping-down-as-head-coach-of-saints-after-15-seasons |access-date=January 25, 2022 |archive-date=January 25, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220125190112/https://www.nfl.com/news/sean-payton-stepping-down-as-head-coach-of-saints-after-15-seasons |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rose |first=Bob |title=Report: Saints Head Coach Sean Payton Retiring |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/saints/news/saints-sean-payton-retires |access-date=February 13, 2022 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en |date=January 25, 2022 |archive-date=February 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220211135720/https://www.si.com/nfl/saints/news/saints-sean-payton-retires |url-status=live }}</ref>

This is his second head coaching position; he had previously served as head coach of the [[Las Vegas Raiders|Oakland Raiders]] from {{Nfly|2012|2014}}, with a record of {{Winpct|8|28|record=y}} and no playoff appearances.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 8, 2022 |title=Dennis Allen named head coach of the New Orleans Saints |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/dennis-allen-named-head-coach-new-orleans-saints |website=NewOrleansSaints.com |access-date=June 2, 2023 |archive-date=April 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230404022505/https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/dennis-allen-named-head-coach-new-orleans-saints |url-status=live }}</ref>

This is his first head coaching position.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=January 28, 2022 |title=Giants hire Brian Daboll as head coach |url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-hire-brian-daboll-as-head-coach |access-date=January 28, 2022 |website=Giants.com |archive-date=January 28, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220128235949/https://www.giants.com/news/giants-hire-brian-daboll-as-head-coach |url-status=live }}</ref>

| style="text-align:center;" | Retired
| Arians announced his retirement on March 30 after three seasons with the Buccaneers. During his tenure, the Buccaneers were {{Winpct|31|18|record=y}} with two playoff appearances including one [[NFC South]] title, the [[Super Bowl LV]] title, and a playoff record of {{Winpct|5|1|record=y}}. Arians had previously retired following the {{NFL Year|2017}} season after five seasons with the [[Arizona Cardinals]], spending one year as a commentator for [[NFL on CBS|CBS]] before returning to coaching.
Bowles, who spent the previous three seasons as the Buccaneers' defensive coordinator, was promoted the same day. This is his third head coaching position; he had previously served as interim head coach of the [[Miami Dolphins]] for the last three weeks of the {{nfly|2011}} season, and as head coach of the [[New York Jets]] from {{nfly|2015|2018}}, with a combined record of {{Winpct|26|41|record=y}} and no playoff appearances.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=March 30, 2022 |title=Bruce Arians stepping down as Buccaneers head coach; Todd Bowles to succeed him |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bruce-arians-retiring-as-buccaneers-head-coach-todd-bowles-to-succeed-him |access-date=March 30, 2022 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=March 31, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220331005202/https://www.nfl.com/news/bruce-arians-retiring-as-buccaneers-head-coach-todd-bowles-to-succeed-him |url-status=live }}</ref>

We Have Questions.|url=https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/the-colts-hired-jeff-saturday-as-head-coach-we-have-questions/|website=[[FiveThirtyEight]]|date=November 10, 2022|access-date=November 10, 2022|archive-date=November 10, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221110161906/https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/the-colts-hired-jeff-saturday-as-head-coach-we-have-questions/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He was the COO of NFL International from 2019 until the hiring.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/34384585/denver-broncos-name-nfl-executive-damani-leech-new-team-president |title=Denver Broncos name NFL executive Damani Leech new team president |date=August 11, 2022 |access-date=August 11, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=August 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220811183043/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/34384585/denver-broncos-name-nfl-executive-damani-leech-new-team-president |url-status=live }}</ref>

After about 19 years with the Raiders including one season as president, Ventrelle was fired on May 6. Ventrelle alleged he was fired for reporting a hostile work environment.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Raiders announce Dan Ventrelle no longer with organization; former interim president alleges he was fired for reporting hostile work environment |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/raiders-announce-president-dan-ventrelle-no-longer-with-organization |website=NFL.com |date=May 6, 2022 |access-date=May 6, 2022 |archive-date=May 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220506183617/https://www.nfl.com/news/raiders-announce-president-dan-ventrelle-no-longer-with-organization |url-status=live }}</ref>

Douglass Morgan was hired on July 7. She previously served as chairwoman of the [[Nevada Gaming Control Board]] from 2019 to 2020. She is the first black female president in NFL history.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/raiders-hire-sandra-douglass-morgan-as-team-president-first-black-woman-president |title=Raiders hire Sandra Douglass Morgan as team president; first Black female president in NFL history |last=Bergman |first=Jeremy |date=July 7, 2022 |access-date=July 7, 2022 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

He previously served as the vice president of football operations for the [[Cleveland Browns]] from 2020 to 2021 and also served for the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in football research and development.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 26, 2022 |title=Kwesi Adofo-Mensah Named New Vikings General Manager |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/kwesi-adofo-mensah-general-manager-announced |access-date=January 26, 2022 |website=Vikings.com |archive-date=January 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220127020803/https://www.vikings.com/news/kwesi-adofo-mensah-general-manager-announced |url-status=live }}</ref>

Schoen was hired on January 21. | style="text-align:center;" |{{sortname|Omar|Khan|dab=American football}}
| After eleven years as the Steelers GM, six years additionally as vice president, and 22 years total with the team in various executive roles, Colbert retired after the [[2022 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Steelers GM Kevin Colbert to step down after 2022 NFL Draft |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/steelers-gm-kevin-colbert-to-step-down-after-2022-nfl-draft |access-date=January 28, 2022 |website=NFL.com |author=Goodbread, Chase |date=January 28, 2022 |archive-date=January 28, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220128192632/https://www.nfl.com/news/steelers-gm-kevin-colbert-to-step-down-after-2022-nfl-draft |url-status=live }}</ref>
Khan was hired on May 25. He has served in various roles with the Steelers for 21 years, most recently as the vice president of football and business administration since 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Steelers officially name Omar Khan new general manager |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/steelers-expected-to-name-omar-khan-new-general-manager |access-date=May 25, 2022 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=May 25, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220525015838/https://www.nfl.com/news/steelers-expected-to-name-omar-khan-new-general-manager |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 20 seasons as the manager of the [[New York Yankees]] (1992–1995), [[Arizona Diamondbacks]] (1998–2000), [[Texas Rangers (baseball)|Texas Rangers]] (2003–2006), and [[Baltimore Orioles]] (2010–2018), Showalter compiled a {{Winpct|1,551|1,517|record=y}} record, with two division titles, five playoff appearances with a playoff record of {{Winpct|9|14|record=y}}, only advancing past the [[Division Series|division series]] once in [[2014 American League Championship Series|2014]].<ref>{{cite news|last=DiComo|first=Anthony|title=Mets announce Showalter as new manager|url=https://www.mlb.com/mets/news/buck-showalter-mets-manager|publisher=[[MLB Advanced Media]]|location=[[New York City|New York]]|date=December 18, 2021|access-date=December 18, 2021|archive-date=December 26, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211226151921/https://www.mlb.com/mets/news/buck-showalter-mets-manager|url-status=live}}</ref>

|[[Bob Melvin]]

Melvin was hired on November 1. He was previously the manager of the [[Seattle Mariners]] (2003–2004), [[Arizona Diamondbacks]] (2005–2009), and the [[Oakland Athletics]] (2011–2021), with a combined record of {{Winpct|1,346|1,272|record=y}}, with seven playoff appearances, a playoff record of {{Winpct|10|17|record=y}}, never advancing past the [[Division Series]].<ref name="Melvin">{{Cite news|last=Cassavell|first=AJ|title=Padres make Bob Melvin next skipper|url=https://www.mlb.com/padres/news/padres-hire-bob-melvin-as-manager|location=[[San Diego]]|publisher=[[MLB Advanced Media]]|date=November 1, 2021|access-date=November 2, 2021|archive-date=November 2, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211102000819/https://www.mlb.com/padres/news/padres-hire-bob-melvin-as-manager|url-status=live}}</ref>

|[[Mike Shildt]]
|[[Oliver Marmol]]
| style="text-align:left;" | On October 14, 2021, Shildt was fired as manager of the Cardinals due to "philosophical differences" according to team president [[John Mozeliak]]. He was voted [[Major League Baseball Manager of the Year Award|National League Manager of the Year]] after the 2019 season.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Silver|first=Zachary|title=Shildt out as Cardinals manager|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/mike-shildt-dismissed-by-cardinals|location=[[New York City|New York]]|publisher=[[MLB Advanced Media]]|date=October 14, 2021|access-date=October 14, 2021|archive-date=October 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211014185350/https://www.mlb.com/news/mike-shildt-dismissed-by-cardinals|url-status=live}}</ref>

This is his first managerial position.<ref>{{Cite news|last1=Landry|first1=Kennedi|last2=Vedia|first2=Arianna|title=Rangers part ways with Chris Woodward|url=https://www.mlb.com/rangers/news/chris-woodward-rangers-part-ways|location=[[Arlington, Texas|Arlington]]|publisher=[[MLB Advanced Media]]|date=August 15, 2022|access-date=August 15, 2022|archive-date=August 15, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220815175924/https://www.mlb.com/rangers/news/chris-woodward-rangers-part-ways|url-status=live}}</ref>

On October 21, the Rangers announced Bruce Bochy as the 20th manager in franchise history, signing a three-year deal. In 25 seasons as the manager of the [[San Diego Padres]] (1995–2006), and [[San Francisco Giants]] (2007–2019), Bochy compiled a record of {{Winpct|2,003|2,029|record=y}} with six division titles, eight playoff appearances, and a playoff record of {{Winpct|44|33|record=y}}, winning three World Series championships with the Giants.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/rangers/2022/10/21/rangers-name-three-time-world-series-champion-bruce-bochy-as-next-manager/|last=Grant|first=Evan|title=Rangers hire three-time World Series champion Bruce Bochy as next manager|newspaper=[[Dallas Morning News]]|location=[[Dallas]]|date=October 22, 2022|archive-date=October 21, 2022|access-date=October 21, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221021171431/https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/rangers/2022/10/21/rangers-name-three-time-world-series-champion-bruce-bochy-as-next-manager/|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-

| style="text-align:left;" | On August 31, White Sox manager Tony La Russa was ruled out indefinitely after undergoing tests on his heart. La Russa would be ruled to not return for the season on September 24 with encouragement from his doctors. On October 3, La Russa announced he would step away from managing.
Cairo, the current bench coach, was named as the interim manager on the same day La Russa was first ruled out on August 31. This is his first managerial position.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/tony-la-russa-away-from-white-sox-indefinitely|title=La Russa away from club indefinitely amid medical tests|first=Scott|last=Merkin|publisher=[[MLB Advanced Media]]|location=[[New York City|New York]]|date=August 31, 2022|access-date=September 4, 2022|archive-date=September 4, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220904194901/https://www.mlb.com/news/tony-la-russa-away-from-white-sox-indefinitely|url-status=live}}</ref>

| Robinson was fired on December 6, 2022, after more than six seasons as the Titans' GM, despite a relatively successful tenure with the Titans, including two AFC South titles, four playoff appearances, and an AFC Championship appearance in 2019.
Cowden, the team's vice president of player personnel, served as interim GM for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web |author=Davenport, Turron|date=December 6, 2022|title=Titans fire GM Jon Robinson despite winning ways |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/35196043/titans-fire-gm-jon-robinson-winning-ways |access-date=December 6, 2022 |website=[[ESPN]] |archive-date=December 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221211172523/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/35196043/titans-fire-gm-jon-robinson-winning-ways |url-status=live }}</ref>

Carthon was hired on January 18. He had been in management positions with several teams since 2008, after playing two seasons with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] from 2004 to 2006. His most recent position was as the [[San Francisco 49ers]]' director of pro/player personnel since 2017.<ref>{{cite web|last=Wyatt|first=Jim|title=Titans Hire Former 49ers Director of Player Personnel Ran Carthon as the Team's New General Manager|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-hire-former-49ers-director-of-player-personnel-ran-carthon-as-the-team-s-|website=tennesseetitans.com|date=January 18, 2023|access-date=January 18, 2023|archive-date=January 18, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230118154535/https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-hire-former-49ers-director-of-player-personnel-ran-carthon-as-the-team-s-|url-status=live}}</ref>

|style="text-align:left;"|On July 13, 2022, after losing 10 of their last 13 games, the Blue Jays fired Montoyo. This is his first managerial position.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Kreuz|first=Julia|title=Blue Jays dismiss manager Charlie Montoyo|url=https://www.mlb.com/bluejays/news/charlie-montoyo-dismissed-by-blue-jays|publisher=[[MLB Advanced Media]]|location=[[Toronto]]|date=July 13, 2022|access-date=July 13, 2022|archive-date=July 13, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220713184325/https://www.mlb.com/bluejays/news/charlie-montoyo-dismissed-by-blue-jays|url-status=live}}</ref>

Beasley, the third-base coach, was appointed the interim manager on the same day.
