|style="text-align:left;"|On October 2, 2022, the White Sox announced that La Russa would retire because of health issues. He guided them to the 2021 AL Central Division title, making his only postseason appearance with the team in his second stint.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://chicagotribune.com/sports/chicago-white-sox/chicago-white-sox-manager-tony-la-russa-retires|title=Chicago White Sox Manager Tony La Russa Retires|website=Chicagotribune.com|date=October 3, 2022|access-date=October 3, 2022}} {{Dead link|date=September 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>
Grifol was hired on November 1. Previously an assistant coach for the [[Kansas City Royals]], this is his first managerial position.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/pedro-grifol-white-sox-manager|title=White Sox name Pedro Grifol as manager|publisher=[[MLB Advanced Media]]|access-date=November 3, 2022|archive-date=November 14, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221114191418/https://www.mlb.com/news/pedro-grifol-white-sox-manager|url-status=live}}</ref>

|[[Mike Matheny]]
|None
|Fired
|[[Matt Quatraro]]
|style="text-align:left;"|On October 5, 2022, hours after the season ended, the Royals announced that Matheny would not return to the team for a fourth season after three years with the team and no playoff appearances.<ref name=":1">{{cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/mlb/news/royals-fire-manager-mike-matheny-after-three-disappointing-seasons-at-the-helm|title=Royals Fire Manager Mike Matheny After Three Disappointing Seasons At The Helm|website=CBSSports.com|date=October 5, 2022|accessdate=October 5, 2022}}</ref> Matheny ended his three-year tenure with a record of {{Winning percentage|165|219|record=y}}.
On October 30, Tampa Bay Rays bench coach Matt Quatraro was named the new manager of the team.<ref>{{cite news|last=Rogers|first=Anne|title=Royals hire Matt Quatraro as next manager|url=https://www.mlb.com/royals/news/matt-quatraro-next-royals-manager|publisher=[[MLB Advanced Media]]|location=[[Kansas City, Missouri|Kansas City]]|date=October 30, 2022|access-date=October 30, 2022|archive-date=January 17, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240117085028/https://www.mlb.com/royals/news/matt-quatraro-next-royals-manager|url-status=live}}</ref> This is his first managerial position.

!Interim
!New
!Reason |- | [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] | [[Eric Musselman]] | | [[John Calipari]] |Musselman left Arkansas after 5 seasons to take the USC job on April 4, 2024.{{cite press release|url=https://usctrojans.com/news/2024/4/4/musselman-named-usc-mens-basketball-head-coach.aspx|title=Eric Musselman Named USC Men's Basketball Head Coach|publisher=USC Trojans|date=April 4, 2024|access-date=April 4, 2024}} On April 10, the Razorbacks announced that former Kentucky head coach and Hall-of-Famer John Calipari will take over as their next men's basketball coach.{{cite press release|url=https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/hall-of-fame-coach-john-calipari-to-lead-razorback-basketball/|title=Hall of Fame Coach John Calipari To Lead Razorback Basketball|publisher=Arkansas Razorbacks|date=April 10, 2024|access-date=April 10, 2024}} |- |[[Bryant Bulldogs men's basketball|Bryant]] |[[Jared Grasso]] |colspan="2" style="text-align:center;"|[[Phil Martelli Jr.]] |Grasso, who had been on a leave of absence from Bryant since September, with the school providing no more information as to why, announced his resignation on November 13, 2023 after 5 seasons. Bulldogs associate head coach Phil Martelli Jr., who was named acting head coach during Grasso's initial leave, was set to continue in that role for the rest of the season{{Cite web |title=Bryant coach Jared Grasso resigning after leave of absence |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/38889396/bryant-coach-jared-grasso-resigning-leave-absence|website=ESPN.com|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|date=November 13, 2023|access-date=November 13, 2023}} until 2 days later when he was officially named the new head coach of the program.{{cite press release|url=https://www.bryantbulldogs.com/sports/mbkb/2023-24/releases/20231114wa1yfe|title=Bryant names Phil Martelli Jr. head men's basketball coach|publisher=Bryant Bulldogs|date=November 15, 2023|access-date=November 16, 2023}} |- |[[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]] |[[Mark Pope]] | |[[Kevin Young (basketball, born 1981)|Kevin Young]] |On April 12, 2024, Pope left BYU after 5 seasons with a 110–52 record to become the head coach at his alma mater, the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|University of Kentucky]].{{cite press release|url=https://ukathletics.com/news/2024/04/12/mark-pope-named-head-coach-of-kentucky-mens-basketball/|title=Mark Pope Named Head Coach of Kentucky Men's Basketball|publisher=Kentucky Wildcats|date=April 12, 2024|access-date=April 12, 2024}} [[Phoenix Suns]] associate head coach Young was hired by the Cougars on April 16.{{cite news|url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2024/04/16/byu-basketball-hires-kevin-young-head-coach/|title=BYU to hire Phoenix Suns assistant Kevin Young as its new head basketball coach|newspaper=[[Deseret News]]|first=Jackson|last=Payne|date=April 16, 2024|access-date=April 16, 2024}} |- | [[Cal Poly Mustangs men's basketball|Cal Poly]] | [[John Smith (basketball, born 1969)|John Smith]] | | [[Mike DeGeorge]] | Cal Poly announced on March 1, 2024 that Smith would not return at the end of the season, ending his 5-year tenure at the school. Under Smith, the Mustangs were 30–117 overall, having lost at least 20 games in all seasons under Smith.{{cite press release|url=https://gopoly.com/news/2024/3/1/mens-basketball-cal-poly-to-part-ways-with-john-smith-at-seasons-end.aspx|title=Cal Poly to Part Ways with John Smith at Season's End|publisher=Cal Poly This was his first head coaching position.<ref name="Smith-Wooden">{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Chargers Name Giff Smith Interim Head Coach and JoJo Wooden Interim General Manager|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-name-giff-smith-interim-head-coach-and-jojo-wooden-interim-gm-2023|website=chargers.com|date=December 15, 2023|access-date=December 15, 2023|archive-date=September 14, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240914173156/https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-name-giff-smith-interim-head-coach-and-jojo-wooden-interim-gm-2023|url-status=live}}</ref> He finished the season with an {{winpct|record=y|0|3}} record.

Harbaugh was hired on January 24. This is his second NFL coaching position, previously coaching the [[San Francisco 49ers]] from {{nfly|2011|2014}}, leading them to two [[NFC West]] division titles, three consecutive [[NFC Championship Game]] appearances and a [[Super Bowl XLVII|Super Bowl]] appearance, ending his tenure with a regular season record of {{winpct|record=y|44|19|1}}. He was most recently the head coach at [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan]] from [[2015 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2015]]–[[2023 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2023]], leading the Wolverines to three [[College Football Playoff]] appearances and a National Championship in [[2024 College Football Playoff National Championship|2023]]. His college experience also included stints at [[San Diego Toreros football|San Diego]] and [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford]], and his overall college record was {{winpct|record=y|144|52}}.<ref>{{cite web |title=Los Angeles Chargers Agree to Terms with Jim Harbaugh as Head Coach |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-name-jim-harbaugh-michigan-head-coach |website=chargers.com |date=January 24, 2024 |access-date=January 24, 2024 |archive-date=January 25, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240125011810/https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-name-jim-harbaugh-michigan-head-coach |url-status=live }}</ref>
|-
! scope="row" style="text-align:center;" | [[New England Patriots]]
| style="text-align:center;" colspan="2" | {{sortname|Bill|Belichick}}
| style="text-align:center;" | {{sortname|Jerod|Mayo}}
| style="text-align:center;" | Mutual agreement
|On January 11, Belichick and the Patriots mutually agreed to part ways after 24 seasons together. In that period, the team compiled a regular season record of {{Winpct|266|121|record=y}}, winning the [[AFC East]] division title 17 times with 18 overall playoff appearances. In the post-season, the team compiled a record of {{Winpct|30|12|record=y}}, with 13 [[AFC Championship Game]] appearances, nine Super Bowl appearances, and six Super Bowl championships ([[Super Bowl XXXVI|XXXVI]], [[Super Bowl XXXVIII|XXXVIII]], [[Super Bowl XXXIX|XXXIX]], [[Super Bowl XLIX|XLIX]], [[Super Bowl LI|LI]], and [[Super Bowl LIII|LIII]]).<ref name="Belichick">{{cite web|title=The Patriots and Bill Belichick Have Mutually Agreed to Part Ways|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/the-patriots-and-bill-belichick-have-mutually-agreed-to-part-ways|website=patriots.com|date=January 11, 2024|access-date=January 11, 2024|archive-date=January 11, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240111171854/https://www.patriots.com/news/the-patriots-and-bill-belichick-have-mutually-agreed-to-part-ways|url-status=live}}</ref>
Mayo was hired on January 12. A Patriots linebacker from 2008 to 2015 ([[Defensive Rookie of the Year]] in [[2008 NFL season|2008]]) and a Patriots defensive coach from 2019 to 2023, this is his first head coaching position at any level.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/analysis-patriots-name-jerod-mayo-as-franchise-s-15th-head-coach |title=Analysis: Patriots Name Jerod Mayo as Franchise's 15th Head Coach |date=January 12, 2024 |website=patriots.com |access-date=January 12, 2024 |archive-date=September 14, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240914173325/https://www.patriots.com/news/analysis-patriots-name-jerod-mayo-as-franchise-s-15th-head-coach |url-status=live }}</ref>
|-
! scope="row" style="text-align:center;" |[[Seattle Seahawks]]
| style="text-align:center;" colspan="2" |{{sortname|Pete|Carroll}}
| style="text-align:center;" | {{sortname|Mike|Macdonald}}
| style="text-align:center;" | Reassigned
|On January 10, Carroll was reassigned to an advisor role after 14 seasons as head coach of the Seahawks. During his tenure, the team was {{Winpct|137|89|1|record=y}}. The team made the playoffs ten times, including five [[NFC West]] division titles, two Super Bowl appearances, the [[Super Bowl XLVIII]] championship, and an overall playoff record of {{Winpct|10|9|record=y}}.<ref>{{cite web|last=Boyle|first=John|title=Pete Carroll To Move Into Advisor Role With Seahawks|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/pete-carroll-to-move-into-advisor-role-with-seahawks|website=seahawks.com|date=January 10, 2024|access-date=January 10, 2024|archive-date=January 15, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240115025205/https://www.seahawks.com/news/pete-carroll-to-move-into-advisor-role-with-seahawks|url-status=live}}</ref>
Macdonald was hired on January 31. A long time Ravens defensive assistant, he was most recently the Ravens' defensive coordinator from {{NFL Year|2022|2023}}. This is his first head coaching position at any level.<ref>{{cite web|last=Boyle|first=John|title=Mike Macdonald Named Head Coach Of The Seattle Seahawks|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/mike-macdonald-named-head-coach-of-the-seattle-seahawks|website=Seahawks.com|date=January 31, 2024|access-date=January 31, 2024|archive-date=September 14, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240914173159/https://www.seahawks.com/news/mike-macdonald-named-head-coach-of-the-seattle-seahawks|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
! scope="row" style="text-align:center;" | [[Tennessee Titans]]
| style="text-align:center;" colspan="2" | {{sortname|Mike|Vrabel|}}
| style="text-align:center;" |{{sortname|Brian|Callahan}}
| rowspan="2" style="text-align:center;" | Fired
| On January 9, Vrabel was fired after six seasons with the Titans. During his tenure, the team was {{Winpct|54|45|record=y}}, with two [[AFC South]] division titles in three overall playoff appearances, and a playoff record of {{Winpct|2|3|record=y}}.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |title=Titans Part Ways With Head Coach Mike Vrabel |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-part-ways-with-head-coach-mike-vrabel |website=Tennessee Titans |date=January 9, 2024 |access-date=January 9, 2024 |archive-date=January 13, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240113084340/https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-part-ways-with-head-coach-mike-vrabel |url-status=live }}</ref>
Callahan was hired on January 24. A long time offensive assistant for several teams, he was most recently the Cincinnati Bengals' offensive coordinator from {{nfly|2019|2023}}. This is his first head coaching position at any level.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |title=Titans Hire Brian Callahan for Head Coaching Job |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-hire-brian-callahan-for-head-coaching-job |website=Tennessee Titans |date=January 24, 2024 |access-date=January 24, 2024 |archive-date=January 24, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240124153443/https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-hire-brian-callahan-for-head-coaching-job |url-status=live }}</ref>
|-
! scope="row" style="text-align:center;" | [[Washington Commanders]]
| style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| {{sortname|Ron|Rivera}}
| style="text-align:center;" | {{sortname|Dan|Quinn|link=Dan Quinn (American football)}}
| On January 8, Rivera was fired after four seasons with the Commanders. During his tenure, the team was {{Winpct|26|40|1|record=y}}, with one playoff appearance and no playoff wins.<ref>{{cite web|last=Selby|first=Zach|title=Commanders part ways with Ron Rivera as head coach|url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-part-ways-with-ron-rivera-as-head-coach|publisher=[[Washington Commanders]]|date=January 8, 2024|access-date=January 8, 2024|archive-date=January 8, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240108141338/https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-part-ways-with-ron-rivera-as-head-coach|url-status=live}}</ref>
Quinn was hired on February 3. This is his second head coaching position, previously coaching the [[Atlanta Falcons]] from {{nfly|2015|2020}}, leading them to two playoff appearances and a [[Super Bowl LI|Super Bowl]] appearance, ending his tenure with a regular season record of {{winpct|record=y|43|42}}. He was most recently the defensive coordinator of the [[Dallas Cowboys]] from {{nfly|2021|2023}}, with his unit leading the league in takeaways all three years.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dan Quinn Named Washington Commanders' 31st Head Coach |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/dan-quinn-named-washington-commanders-31st-head-coach |website=Commanders.com |date=February 3, 2024 |access-date=February 3, 2024 |archive-date=February 11, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240211164710/https://www.commanders.com/news/dan-quinn-named-washington-commanders-31st-head-coach |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Epstein |first1=Jori |title=In new opportunity with Commanders and Jayden Daniels, Dan Quinn is checking his blind spots |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/in-new-opportunity-with-commanders-and-jayden-daniels-dan-quinn-is-checking-his-blind-spots-220537686.html |website=Yahoo |date=June 25, 2024 |access-date=July 4, 2024 |archive-date=July 9, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240709194941/https://sports.yahoo.com/in-new-opportunity-with-commanders-and-jayden-daniels-dan-quinn-is-checking-his-blind-spots-220537686.html |url-status=live }}</ref>
|}

|Reassigned

|style="text-align:left;"|On September 14, 2023, O'Halloran accepted the position of senior vice president of baseball operations with the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2023/09/22/sports/brian-ohalloran-red-sox/|title=Brian O'Hallon Accepts Position As Red Sox Executive VP Of Baseball Operations|website=BostonGolbe.com|date=September 22, 2023|accessdate=September 22, 2023|author1=Speier, Alex|author2=McWilliams, Julian|archive-date=September 22, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230922182654/https://www.bostonglobe.com/2023/09/22/sports/brian-ohalloran-red-sox/|url-status=live}}</ref>

|[[Billy Eppler]]
|rowspan=2|Resigned
|[[David Stearns]]
|style="text-align:left;"|On October 5, 2023, Eppler resigned as general manager as a result of MLB opening an investigation into his potentially improper use of the injured list.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/mets/news/billy-eppler-steps-down-as-mets-general-manager|title=Eppler steps down as Mets general manager|website=[[MLB.com]]|date=October 5, 2023|accessdate=October 6, 2023|archive-date=October 5, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231005233632/https://www.mlb.com/mets/news/billy-eppler-steps-down-as-mets-general-manager|url-status=live}}</ref>

|[[Kim Ng]]
|[[Peter Bendix]]
|style="text-align:left;"|On October 16, 2023, Ng resigned as general manager after three years. |style="text-align:left;"|On September 29, 2023, the Giants fired Kapler. After four seasons with the team, he compiled a record of {{Winning percentage|295|248|record=y}} and made the playoffs once in 2021.
Bench coach Kai Correa was named interim manager for the final three games of the 2023 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/mlb/san-francisco-giants/giants-fire-manager-gabe-kapler-after-disapointing-2023-mlb-season|title=Giants Fire Manager Gabe Kapler After Disappointing 2023 season|website=NBCSportsbayarea.com|date=September 29, 2023|accessdate=September 29, 2023|archive-date=July 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240706230843/https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/mlb/san-francisco-giants/|url-status=live}}</ref> Melvin was hired on October 25. | rowspan="7" |N/A
| [[Carlos Mendoza (baseball coach)|Carlos Mendoza]]
|style="text-align:left;"|On October 1, 2023, Showalter announced he would not return to manage the Mets for the 2024 season. According to team owner [[Steve Cohen (businessman)|Steve Cohen]] and general manager [[Billy Eppler]], the Mets informed Showalter that they did not plan to bring him back for next season, even though he had one year left on his contract. He compiled a record of {{Winning percentage|176|148|record=y}} in two seasons with the team with one playoff appearance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/mets/news/buck-showalter-will-not-manage-mets-in-2024|title=Showalter will not return as Mets' manager in 2024|website=[[MLB.com]]|date=October 1, 2023|accessdate=October 1, 2023|archive-date=October 2, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231002012349/https://www.mlb.com/mets/news/buck-showalter-will-not-manage-mets-in-2024|url-status=live}}</ref>
On November 13, Yankees bench coach Carlos Mendoza was named the new manager of the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/mets/news/carlos-mendoza-mets-manager|title=Mets hire Mendoza from Yankees as next manager|website=[[MLB.com]]|access-date=November 13, 2023|archive-date=November 13, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231113185820/https://www.mlb.com/mets/news/carlos-mendoza-mets-manager|url-status=live}}</ref>

|[[Phil Nevin]]
|Option not picked up
|[[Ron Washington]]
| style="text-align:left;" |On October 2, 2023, the Angels announced they would not be picking up Nevin's option for 2024. After taking over as manager in June 2022, he compiled a record of {{Winning percentage|119|149|record=y}} with no playoff appearances.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/angels/news/phil-nevin-will-not-return-as-angels-manager|title=Phil Nevin Will Not Return As Angels Manager|website=MLB.com|date=October 2, 2023|accessdate=October 2, 2023|archive-date=October 3, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231003132353/https://www.mlb.com/angels/news/phil-nevin-will-not-return-as-angels-manager|url-status=live}}</ref>
Washington was hired on November 8. This will be his second managerial position, previously managing Texas from 2007 to 2014, going {{Winpct|664|611|record=y}} and winning the AL pennant in back-to-back seasons in 2010 and 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/angels-hire-ron-washington-as-manager|title=Angels hire Ron Washington as manager|website=MLB.com|date=November 8, 2023|accessdate=November 8, 2023}}{{Dead link|date=September 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

| style="text-align:left;" |On October 3, 2023, Francona announced he was stepping away as manager of the Guardians. In 11 seasons with Cleveland, he compiled a record of {{Winning percentage|921|757|record=y}} with six playoff appearances, three [[American League Central|AL Central]] division titles, and a [[2016 World Series|World Series]] appearance.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 3, 2023 |title=Guardians manager Terry Francona announces he's stepping away from Guardians |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/guardians-manager-terry-francona-announces-hes-stepping-away-from-guardians-182816034.html |access-date=October 3, 2023 |work=Yahoo Sports|author=Roscher, Liz}}</ref>
Vogt was hired on November 6. This will be his first managerial position.<ref>{{cite web|last=Bell|first=Mandy|title=Former Catcher Stephen Vogt Named Guardians Skipper|url=https://www.mlb.com/former/guardians/catcher/stephen/vogt/named/next/guardians/manager|website=MLB.com|date=November 6, 2023|accessdate=November 6, 2023}}{{Dead link|date=September 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

In his tenure with the Padres, he compiled a record of {{Winning percentage|171|153|record=y}}, with one playoff appearance, advancing to the [[National League Championship Series|NLCS]] in 2022.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Guardado|first=Maria|title=Giants officially name Melvin next manager|url=https://www.mlb.com/giants/news/bob-melvin-giants-manager|website=MLB.com|date=October 25, 2023|access-date=October 25, 2023|archive-date=October 28, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231028053521/https://www.mlb.com/giants/news/bob-melvin-giants-manager|url-status=live}}</ref>

This will be his second managerial position.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Cassavell|first1=AJ|title=Padres name Mike Shildt as manager with 2-year contract|url=https://www.mlb.com/padres/news/san-diego-padres-mike-shildt-manager|website=MLB.com|date=November 21, 2023|access-date=November 21, 2023|archive-date=November 21, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231121205213/https://www.mlb.com/padres/news/san-diego-padres-mike-shildt-manager|url-status=live}}</ref>

|[[Dusty Baker]]
|Retired
|[[Joe Espada]]
|style="text-align:left;"|On October 25, 2023, Baker announced his retirement after four seasons with the Astros and 26 years overall as a manager. He finished his tenure with the Astros with a {{Winning percentage|320|226|record=y}} record, winning the 2022 World Series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/mlb/columnist/bob-nightengale/2023/10/25/dusty-baker-retires/71302675007/|title=Exclusive: Dusty Baker retires after 26 seasons as MLB manager|work=USA Today|first=Bob|last=Nightengale|date=October 25, 2023|accessdate=October 25, 2023|archive-date=July 6, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240706231425/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/mlb/columnist/bob-nightengale/2023/10/25/dusty-baker-retires/71302675007/|url-status=live}}</ref>
On November 13, Joe Espada was named the new manager of the team. This is his first managerial position.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/astros/houston-astros-name-joe-espada-the-new-manager|title=Houston Astros Name Joe Espada The New Manager|website=Houstonchronicle.com|date=November 13, 2023|accessdate=November 13, 2023}}{{Dead link |date=July 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Astros name Joe Espada as new manager|date=November 13, 2023|access-date=July 14, 2024|url=https://www.mlb.com/press-release/press-release-astros-name-joe-espada-as-new-manager|website=mlb.com|archive-date=September 17, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240917072630/https://www.mlb.com/press-release/press-release-astros-name-joe-espada-as-new-manager|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
!scope="row" style="text-align:center;"|[[Chicago Cubs]]
|[[David Ross (baseball)|David Ross]]
|Fired
|[[Craig Counsell]]
|style="text-align:left;"|On November 6, 2023, the Cubs fired Ross after four seasons. He finished his tenure with a {{Winning percentage|262|284|record=y}} record, with one playoff appearance, winning the [[National League Central|NL Central]] in the 2020 season.
Counsell was hired on the same day. As the Brewers manager, he compiled a record of {{Winning percentage|707|625|record=y}}, with three [[National League Central|NL Central]] division titles and five overall playoff appearances.<ref>{{cite web|last=Bastian|first=Jordan|title=Cubs hire Counsell as new manager|url=https://www.mlb.com/cubs/news/craig-counsell-new-cubs-manager|website=MLB.com|date=November 6, 2023|accessdate=November 6, 2023|archive-date=November 6, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231106204511/https://www.mlb.com/cubs/news/craig-counsell-new-cubs-manager|url-status=live}}</ref>
|-
!scope="row" style="text-align:center;"|[[Milwaukee Brewers]]
|[[Craig Counsell]]
|Contract expired
|[[Pat Murphy (baseball coach)|Pat Murphy]] 
|style="text-align:left;"|Counsell's contract with the Brewers expired on November 1, 2023. The Brewers offered a contract extension to Counsell weeks prior before the 53-year-old became a free agent and interviewed with other clubs. Counsell became the manager of the [[Chicago Cubs]] on November 6. As the Brewers manager for nine seasons, he compiled a record of {{Winning percentage|707|625|record=y}}, with three [[National League Central|NL Central]] division titles and five overall playoff appearances.<ref>{{cite web|last=McCalvy|first=Adam|url=https://www.mlb.com/brewers/news/brewers-contract-offer-to-craig-counsell|title=Counsell moving on to division rival|website=MLB.com|date=November 6, 2023|accessdate=November 6, 2023|archive-date=November 6, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231106204513/https://www.mlb.com/brewers/news/brewers-contract-offer-to-craig-counsell|url-status=live}}</ref>
On November 15, Pat Murphy was named the new manager of the team. This will be his second managerial position.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pat Murphy named Brewers manager: Bench coach promoted to top job after Craig Counsell's exit |url=https://www.cbssports.com/mlb/news/pat-murphy-named-brewers-manager-bench-coach-promoted-to-top-job-after-craig-counsells-exit/ |website=cbssports.com |date=November 15, 2023 |access-date=November 15, 2023 |author1=Snyder, Matt |author2=Anderson, R.J. |archive-date=November 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116004815/https://www.cbssports.com/mlb/news/pat-murphy-named-brewers-manager-bench-coach-promoted-to-top-job-after-craig-counsells-exit/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

| [[Terry Francona]]

Shaw, previously an assistant coach, was named interim head coach the same day,{{cite web |title=Flyers relieve John Tortorella of head coaching duties |url=https://www.nhl.com/flyers/news/flyers-relieve-john-tortorella-of-head-coaching-duties |access-date=March 27, 2025 |website=NHL.com |date=March 27, 2025 |archive-date=March 27, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250327152155/https://www.nhl.com/flyers/news/flyers-relieve-john-tortorella-of-head-coaching-duties |url-status=live}} and compiled a 5–3–1 record over the final nine games of the season.
